findings.title: Flattening error at FLATTEN_STEPS=24 quantified: worst 16.0 um at 1 in cap — academic vs kerf, faint faceting only at extreme Corel zoom
findings.evidence: Measured max chordal deviation of the 24-step polyline from the true Beziers on the UNITED cut path (doc.cut_skia, the exact curves the exporter flattens; nameplate_core.py:47, :511-575), 6 names x 3 shipped fonts at 1 in cap. Merriweather (quads, cap_ref=1486): worst 0.127 fu = 2.16 um. TGCarrieSO (cubics): worst 0.253 fu = 4.48 um. TGCarrieSOFlourish: worst 0.902 fu = 16.0 um (ADAM, flourish sweep). Cross-validated independently in a second experiment (dense curve samples vs shipped polyline: 16.00 um, same number). Kerf is 100-200 um, so worst error is 8-16% of the SMALL kerf; CorelDRAW precision is 0.0001 in = 2.54 um, so faceting is detectable only when zoomed far in. Chords lie inside convex curve spans, so the bias is a local undersize of at most 16 um.
findings.proposed_fix: No fix required for cutting accuracy. Record the measured bound (16 um at 1 in cap, scales linearly with cap height) in SPEC.md so future changes to FLATTEN_STEPS have a reference number, and use it as the acceptance threshold for the EF-2 curve exporter's equivalence test.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on cut parts: 16 um max local deviation is far under kerf and under Corel hairline width (25.4 um). Purely a representation-precision statement.
findings.risk: None — documentation only. acceptance_tests.py (53) unaffected.

findings.title: True-curve SVG export is viable in nameplate_export.py: byte-identical header/viewBox, 13-21% file size, representation error drops 16 um -> ~1.3 um
findings.evidence: Prototype (scratch, no app file touched): walked doc.cut_skia (build_document already stores the curve-preserving union, nameplate_core.py:248, :431-439) and emitted SVG C/Q segments with the exact svg_single transform (sx=sy=doc.scale, ox=x0, oy=y1). Results for ADAM: header lines (width/height/viewBox/comment) byte-identical to shipped output in both fonts tested; true-curve artwork exceeds the polyline-derived viewBox by at most 1.04 um (Flourish right edge) — invisible under the 25.4 um hairline stroke. MERRI: 3,368 B vs 15,946 B (21.1%), 188 coordinate pairs vs 1,024. FLOURISH: 11,616 B vs 88,377 B (13.1%), 772 vs 5,859. Raster diff (QSvgRenderer 2400x600): only antialiasing-level differences (0.35-2.0% pixels), no structural change. Contour order in cut_skia is 1:1 with the flattened rings of cut_paths[0] across all 18 font x name cases (firstPoints match ring[0]) — so the ring indices that build_pieces and lead_in_report use map cleanly onto curve contours.
findings.proposed_fix: Live entirely in nameplate_export.py (own 31-test suite), core untouched: (1) build_pieces() gains curves=False kwarg; when True, Piece rows carry segment lists taken from doc.cut_skia.contours (index i = ring i, verified above) and svg()/pdf() gain curve-aware emitters (SVG C/Q; PDF 'c' operator, quads degree-elevated). (2) Lead-ins: keep the ENTIRE search/verify pipeline in nameplate_leadin.py on polylines (unchanged); at emit time map the chosen anchor onto the true curve: re-flatten cut_skia in the exporter recording (segment_index, t=j/24) provenance per vertex, project the anchor to the curve within its chord's t-interval, split that Bezier at t* by de Casteljau (exact), and emit ONE open path: M pierce, L anchor-on-curve, second half of split segment, remaining segments around the ring, first half of split segment, ending at the anchor — pierce->anchor->full contour->anchor preserved, path open, contour length exact. (3) Tests to add: header byte-identity vs polyline export; dense-sample distance curve-vs-polyline <= 16 um/in bound; run invariants (starts at pierce, 2nd point = anchor, ends at anchor, open); node-count reduction sanity; one manual Corel import check per verify_corel.ps1 before flipping any GUI default. Ship default-OFF behind a checkbox.
findings.accuracy_effect: Positive: exported geometry error drops from <=16 um (chord representation) to <=1.3 um (%.4f-inch control-point quantization; curve stays within the convex hull of rounded control points). Cut order, per-name groups, and lead-in merge contract unchanged.
findings.risk: Three real risks: (a) lead-in clearance is verified against the polyline material, which sits up to 16 um inside the true curve on convex spans — the HARD_CLEARANCE floor (0.004 in = 102 um) erodes by up to 16%; mitigate by buffering the _Void material by the 16 um/in bound when curves are on. (b) Downstream laser software must flatten Beziers itself (LightBurn/Corel do, with adaptive tolerance — typically finer than 24 steps). (c) PDF curve emission is new code in the hand-rolled writer. Proof: export_tests.py (31) must stay green with curves=False (default), plus the new curve tests; goldens (53) untouched since core svg_single is never modified.

findings.title: One-shot pathops.union() is NOT byte-identical to the shipped incremental union — geometry equal to 4 nm, but 7/18 SVGs differ; gain is ~0.5-3.5 ms/name; do not ship
findings.evidence: Reproduced build_document's incremental loop (nameplate_core.py:432-439: union = pathops.op(union, piece, UNION) per glyph; verified my reproduction flattens byte-equal to shipped doc.cut_paths), then compared pathops.union(all_pieces) one-shot across 3 fonts x 6 names: 11/18 byte-identical SVGs, 7/18 DIFFERENT. Differences are (a) different curve-subdivision points at glyph intersections (MERRI ADAM: 994 vs 1018 polyline points, coordinate shifts up to 0.83 fu because chords sample the same curve at different parameters), (b) ring start-point rotation (MERRI Carrie/Quinn/Sophia), (c) float noise 1e-14 to 6e-5 fu. Symmetric max vertex distance between the two flattened outlines: 0.0002 fu = 0.004 um — the SHAPES are identical. Timing: one-shot 2.13x faster on the union step, but the union loop is only 0.75 ms (15.4% of a 4.9 ms build) on Merriweather and 6.9 ms (43.5% of 15.8 ms) on Flourish — total win milliseconds per name; a full font check already runs in seconds (regression suite: 10.6 s for 40 names with arrange + lead-ins).
findings.proposed_fix: Skip it. It would break the byte-identical golden SVG regression (acceptance_tests.py) for zero accuracy gain and a speed gain nobody can feel. If ever revisited, it must be a new default-off optional param on build_document with goldens re-verified byte-identical under the default — but the measured benefit does not justify touching the sealed core.
findings.accuracy_effect: Zero if shipped (geometry identical to 4 nm), but output files change bytes — golden regression fails, and repeat jobs would stop being byte-reproducible against archived files.
findings.risk: Shipping it breaks acceptance_tests.py goldens by construction (7/18 cases demonstrated). Not shipping it has no risk.

findings.title: Engrave lines can vanish silently: a band whose segments all fall under MIN_ENGRAVE_LEN (or that sits >ENGRAVE_TOL from the outline) is dropped with NO warning whenever any other band hits; shipped font's thinnest kept segment has only 0.65 fu (11 um) margin
findings.evidence: Semantics (nameplate_core.py:48-49, :445-489): each non-black COLR layer is filled, buffered by ENGRAVE_TOL=1.5 fu, intersected with every flattened outline ring; intersection segments >= MIN_ENGRAVE_LEN=25 fu are kept — the length filter runs BOTH before and after linemerge. The 'none landed' warning (line 484) fires only when engrave is empty AND n_bands>0, i.e. only when EVERY band misses. Proved with a synthetic COLR font run through the real build_document (fontTools.fontBuilder, 6 cases, all PASS): a 21 fu band (24 fu segment, sub-floor) next to a good band produces 1 engrave line and NO warning — the second band vanished silently (case F); same silent vanish for a band 2 fu off the edge (>1.5 tolerance) when another band hits. Live margins on the shipped Merriweather across 11 names: all 62 bands touch their outlines at distance 0.0 fu (full 1.5 fu headroom — healthy), but of 301 raw intersection segments, 71 are dropped sub-floor (mostly ~13 fu) and the smallest KEPT is 25.65 fu — 0.65 fu = 11 um above the floor. Ablating only the PRE-merge filter changes final engrave geometry: individual line ends move up to 12.8 fu = 0.219 mm at 1 in cap, totals change ~0.2% (mixed sign — not a systematic truncation, but proof the filter is load-bearing at kerf scale). 25 fu = 0.427 mm of engrave at 1 in cap: big enough to see on a finished plate.
findings.proposed_fix: Two additive changes plus the tripwire tests. (1) In build_document's engrave block, count per-band contribution (the loop already iterates per band) and append a warning naming the base glyph when a non-empty band yields zero kept segments — pure new-warning addition, no geometry change, goldens stay byte-identical (warnings are not in the SVG). (2) Add engrave_tripwire_tests.py (or extend regression_tests.py) building the verified synthetic font in-memory: glyph 'A' = 600x700 rectangle, 'H' for the cap basis, COLR v0 bands 2 fu tall straddling the top edge, CPAL black+red. Exact recipe validated: kept segment length = band length + 2*ENGRAVE_TOL, glyf coords are INTEGERS, and hmtx lsb must equal each band's xMin or glyf compile slides the band onto the corner. Cases (all verified passing today): band 22 fu -> 25.00 fu segment == floor -> kept; 21 fu -> 24.0 -> dropped + warning; 23 fu -> kept; band gap 1.0 fu < TOL -> kept; gap 2.0 fu > TOL -> dropped + warning; good band + sub-floor band -> 1 line, currently NO warning (this assertion flips when fix (1) lands).
findings.accuracy_effect: Today a font edit or new font can lose a whole engrave line (>= 0.4 mm of visible detail at 1 in cap) with no operator signal; the shipped font is currently safe (all bands hit, 11 um margin on the thinnest segment) but the margin is one font-tweak wide. The fix adds detection only — zero geometry change.
findings.risk: Warning-text additions could trip tests that assert exact warning lists — grep shows acceptance_tests checks specific warphrases, so the new warning must be a new string, not a change to existing ones. Prove with: acceptance_tests.py 53/53 (byte goldens), export_tests.py 31/31, regression_tests.py 12/12 — all confirmed passing on baseline in this audit.

findings.title: PDF layer (OCG) names and /Title destroy non-Latin-1 names: 'Мария' -> '?????', '李明' -> '??' — and different names can collide into identical Corel layer names; SVG keeps them intact
findings.evidence: nameplate_export.py:171-173 (_pdf_escape: .encode('latin-1','replace')) applied to OCG /Name (line 223) and /Title (line 239). Demonstrated: EX.pdf for labels 'Zoë'/'Māra'/'Мария'/'李明' produce OCG names b'Zo\xeb' (fine), b'M?ra', b'?????', b'??' — while the SVG group ids keep 'Māra', 'Мария', '李明' verbatim (_safe_id keeps Unicode alnum, valid XML). Two different 5-letter Cyrillic names both become layer '?????' in CorelDRAW — the per-name layer contract survives structurally but the labels become ambiguous. Geometry is unaffected.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_export.pdf(), emit text strings that latin-1 cannot carry as UTF-16BE with BOM — the PDF-spec form for text strings: if s.encode('latin-1') fails, write (\xFE\xFF + s.encode('utf-16-be')) with the same ()-escaping. Applies to the OCG /Name and /Title objects only; content stream untouched.
findings.accuracy_effect: No cut/engrave geometry change at all; restores name fidelity in Corel's layer panel and prevents identical layer names for different names on one sheet (mis-selection risk for the operator).
findings.risk: UTF-16BE strings in OCG names must be verified once in CorelDRAW import (verify_corel.ps1 flow) — some consumers mishandle them. export_tests.py (31) proves ordering/grouping unchanged; add one test asserting the BOM-prefixed name round-trips out of the written bytes.

findings.title: Coordinate quantization measured: PDF 0.176 um worst (absolute across a 10 in sheet), SVG 1.27 um worst in inch mode — both clean; note the writers' precision is unit-asymmetric
findings.evidence: Built an 8-name sheet 6.919 x 10.421 in via the shipping exporter, decompressed the PDF content stream, parsed all 13,803 coordinates and compared with unrounded recomputation: worst error exactly 0.0005 pt = 0.176 um at coordinates up to 756.3 pt — %.3f (nameplate_export.py:189-190) is absolute quantization, error does NOT grow with sheet size. Same for the SVG (%.4f, line 133): worst exactly 5e-5 in = 1.270 um; in mm mode %.4f gives 5e-5 mm = 0.05 um. Both are 2-3 orders below kerf (100-200 um) and below the 25.4 um hairline. Curves are identical polylines in both formats (same 13,803 points from the same Piece geometry). The 0.0720 w explicit hairline (HAIRLINE_IN*72) is correct and Corel-safe; the core writer's '0 w' device hairline (nameplate_core.py:672) is NOT user-reachable — GUI (nameplate_gui.py:611-635) and CLI (nameplate_cli.py:239-262) both export only through nameplate_export.
findings.proposed_fix: Nothing to fix for geometry. Optional consistency nicety if ever touched: SVG inch-mode precision (1.27 um) is 7x coarser than PDF's — bumping SVG to %.5f would align them, but it changes every exported byte, so leave it unless a file-diff epoch is planned anyway.
findings.accuracy_effect: None today; numbers recorded so 'is rounding hurting us' never needs re-litigating.
findings.risk: Changing SVG precision would alter all exported SVG bytes (customer-facing diff churn) for no measurable physical gain — recommend not doing it.

strengths: All three gating suites pass in this exact environment before and after the audit: acceptance_tests.py 53/53 (byte-identical goldens), export_tests.py 31/31, regression_tests.py 12/12 (10.6 s for 40 names incl. arrange + lead-ins) — a full font check is nowhere near the 1-minute budget.

Flattening does not bias sizing: the cap/x-height basis is measured on FLAT-topped letters whose tops are straight edges, which 24-step flattening reproduces exactly — the 16 um worst curve deviation lives on round/pointed strokes only, so 'HEIT at exactly the asked height' is preserved and J-overshoot semantics are untouched.
The polyline-derived viewBox under-covers the true curves by at most 1.04 um (measured, both fonts) — canvas size math is effectively exact.

The shipped incremental union is geometrically correct: one-shot union agrees to 0.0002 fu (4 nm) across 18 font x name cases; the loop is also byte-reproducible (my independent reimplementation flattened byte-equal to doc.cut_paths in all cases).

cut_skia contour order is 1:1 with the flattened rings of cut_paths[0] in all 18 cases (verified via firstPoints) — the ring indices used by build_pieces and lead_in_report have a clean, already-consistent mapping onto true-curve contours.

Engrave extraction is healthy on the shipped Merriweather: all 62 bands across 11 names sit at distance 0.0 fu from their outlines (full ENGRAVE_TOL headroom), zero bands currently miss, and per-band silent-drop is a latent (not live) hazard.

PDF coordinate quantization is 0.176 um worst-case and absolute — a 10 in sheet is as precise as a 1 in plate; explicit 0.0720 w hairline (not '0 w') is what actually ships, and the device-dependent core PDF writer is unreachable from GUI and CLI.

The lead-in contract (ONE open path: pierce -> anchor -> full contour -> anchor) is enforced in the exporter for both SVG and PDF paths and its per-ring bookkeeping (raw ring index traveling with candidates through merge_run) is correct as documented in nameplate_leadin.py:230-235.

Export cut order (engrave -> inner -> outline last) and per-name grouping are structurally guaranteed by Piece construction order in build_pieces/svg/pdf, independent of any finding here — nothing in this audit touches that contract.

findings.title: First-letter and last-letter joins of real names are never tested; 2 real gaps missed on TGCarrieSOFlourish
findings.evidence: The 5 groups in GROUP_SPECS (nameplate_pairsheet.py:90-101) test whole-2-letter-words (initial->FINAL forms) and mid-word pairs A+l+r+a (medial->medial). A name of length >=3 also uses initial->MEDIAL (link 0-1 of l+r+'a') and medial->FINAL (last link of 'A'+l+r). Experiment (exp3, run from app dir): on TGCarrieSO-v2 and TGCarrieSOFlourish-v2 ALL 1352 initial->medial and ALL 676 medial->final links use glyph pairs that no shipped group ever judges (e.g. 'aba' link0 = Aleftring->b.eng3, vs the tested 'ab' = Aleftring->bflourishrightring.eng3 and mid 'Aaba' = a.eng1->b). Geometry sweep of those links found 2 REAL gaps the whole suite misses: words 'dda' and 'Dda', junction Dleftring->d, gap 1.7 units = 0.00084 em (upem 2048) — the same defect class as the known ADda break, but at the first-letter join. join_scan (nameplate_fontcheck.py:368-410) also misses it: its trigram contexts CONTEXTS='eaonrglstc' (line 365) do not include 'd', and it never varies beyond 10 lowercase initials. On Merriweather the missing-link glyph pairs happen to coincide with tested ones (0 novel), so the hole is font-dependent. Cost of closing it was measured: initial->medial sweep 1352 cells = 0.20-1.35 s, medial->final 676 cells = 0.10-0.22 s (warm cache, slowest font).
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_pairsheet.py, add two (or three) groups to GROUP_SPECS with a new mode handled beside 'middle' in analyse_pairs (line 505-508): mode 'first' shapes left+right+MIDDLE_WRAP[1] and judges the links spanned by clusters 0-1; mode 'last' shapes MIDDLE_WRAP[0]+left+right and judges clusters 1-2. Both reuse the existing _test_middle machinery generalized to a target cluster window (a small refactor of lines 379-457: parametrize the (1,2) at line 407). Additive: new GROUP_SPECS keys, PairResult unchanged, existing groups and their verdicts byte-identical. Add matching rows to PairGrid.ROW_SPECS (nameplate_gui.py:1083-1084) and update the GUI selftest assertion that expects exactly 4 rows per letter (nameplate_gui.py ~3705-3716).
findings.accuracy_effect: Closes the only demonstrated false-clean in the subsystem: a font passing all 3380 current cells can still cut a real name into loose pieces at its first or last join (proven by 'dda'/'Dda' on the shipped flourish font). Adds 2028 measured cells for ~1.6 s on the slowest shipped font (30 s budget has 10x headroom).
findings.risk: GUI selftest (51 checks) asserts keys == ['caplower','lower','midlower','midcaplower'] and 4*26 rows — it must be extended or the new groups must be default-on in analyse_pairs but appended after existing ones. acceptance/export/regression suites never import pairsheet (grep verified), so goldens are untouched. Re-run: GUI --selftest, acceptance_tests.py, export_tests.py, regression_tests.py.

findings.title: UNTESTED cells are invisible in the GUI PairGrid: no ring, no label, excluded from the flagged count
findings.evidence: PairGrid.paintEvent (nameplate_gui.py:1321-1379) draws a red ring and status text only when res.problem is true (line 1328); UNTESTED is not in PROBLEM_STATUSES (nameplate_pairsheet.py:123) and has offsets=() so the cell paints as a blank box with a grey caption — identical to nothing-wrong. flagged_cells()/n_flagged (1145-1157, 1231-1233) skip it, so the dialog headline (1414-1417) counts only problems. The GUI never reads report.budget_hit or n_untested anywhere (grep: 0 hits). Offscreen demonstration (exp6): analyse_pairs(budget_s=0.4) on TGCarrieSOFlourish -> tested=128, untested=3252, problems=1; PairGrid.n_flagged()==1, i.e. the dialog would say '1 pair flagged' while 96% of the sheet was never measured. The module's own contract (pairsheet docstring: 'we did not look can never be mistaken for it passed') is honoured by the CLI summary and the PNG sheets (amber UNTESTED label, _cell_label line 624) but broken by the live GUI grid. Today the GUI default 30 s budget never trips on shipped fonts (full 5-group sweep: 0.8/1.0/3.0 s), so the effect is latent until a heavier font arrives.
findings.proposed_fix: In PairGrid.paintEvent, mirror render_sheet's treatment: amber ring (QPen '#e6960f', 2) and an 'UNTESTED' caption for status=='untested' (add an elif between lines 1328 and 1371), and append 'N untested' in amber to the PairSheetDialog count label when report.n_untested > 0. Purely GUI paint code; nameplate_core and pairsheet untouched.
findings.accuracy_effect: Prevents a starved run from reading as a clean bill in the one place Sean actually looks (the dialog). No verdict changes.
findings.risk: None to goldens or export contract. GUI selftest should gain a check (starved report -> amber count visible). Re-run GUI --selftest.

findings.title: 'caps' group is analysed but cannot be displayed: its failures are missing from the dialog count and navigation
findings.evidence: analyse_pairs defaults to all 5 groups including 'caps' (nameplate_pairsheet.py:102-103) and the GUI calls it with defaults (nameplate_gui.py:3129, 3045). But PairGrid.ROW_SPECS (nameplate_gui.py:1083-1084) lists only caplower/lower/midlower/midcaplower — 'caps' has no row, so its cells can never be seen, stepped to, or counted. Demonstration (exp6): injecting a synthetic GAP into the caps group of a full TGCarrieSOFlourish report gives report problems=4 but PairGrid.n_flagged()=3; claude_prompt() DOES include the caps failure ('A' + 'B' present in the text). So the dialog headline and the paste-ready prompt can disagree, and a real caps break (an all-caps name) would be invisible in the grid while silently present in the prompt. No shipped font currently has a caps failure (all 3 fonts: caps group 0 flagged), so the effect is latent.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ('caps','upper-right') handling to PairGrid: a fifth ROW_SPECS entry ('caps','upper') with right characters uppercased for that group (cols are currently lowercase-only, so PairGrid.result() lookup needs the group-aware right-char case: use right.upper() when group=='caps'). Update the selftest 4-rows assertion. Alternatively, if caps rows are judged not worth the screen space, exclude 'caps' from the two GUI analyse_pairs calls so the dialog count and the prompt describe the same set — but showing it is the accurate option.
findings.accuracy_effect: Makes the dialog count equal the report's failure count; a future all-caps break becomes visible instead of prompt-only.
findings.risk: Row count changes (5x26): GUI selftest assertions on 4*26 rows must be updated; zoom/scroll unaffected (grid is size-driven). Re-run GUI --selftest.

findings.title: _test_middle would return a false OK if a font ever ligated the wrapper with a middle letter (latent; zero occurrences in shipped fonts)
findings.evidence: nameplate_pairsheet.py:407 selects glyphs with cluster in (1,2); lines 438-444 declare lo==hi an OK 'ligature'. If chars 0+1 merged (HarfBuzz gives the ligature cluster 0, cluster 1 absent), idx finds only the cluster-2 glyph, lo==hi, and the pair is declared OK with the middle join never measured. Symmetrically, chars 2+3 merged puts the wrapper's ink inside the 'right' geometry, so wrapper ink could satisfy intersects() and mask a gap at the true join. Exhaustive sweep (exp1): all 4056 wrap words across the 3 shipped fonts shape to exactly 4 glyphs with monotone clusters 0,1,2,3 — no merges of any kind, so this cannot fire today (these fonts use calt alternates, not ligatures). Ground truth (exp2): 4056/4056 middle verdicts match whole-word union connectivity (4055 OK+connected, 1 GAP+disconnected = the known ADda, gap 1.72u/0.00084 em); wrapper ink never bridges a GAP and no GAP's middle-span union was one piece, so adjacency-only judging is exactly right on shipped fonts.
findings.proposed_fix: In _test_middle after computing idx (nameplate_pairsheet.py:407-420): also collect the cluster VALUES present; if 1 is absent while 0 is present, or 2 is absent while a glyph's cluster group spans char 3, return ERROR ('the shaper merged the pair with the wrapper — cannot isolate the middle join') instead of falling through to the lo==hi OK path. ~6 lines, additive, changes no verdict on any current font (verified: zero merges).
findings.accuracy_effect: Converts a hypothetical false PASS into an honest ERROR for future ligature-heavy script fonts. Zero effect on shipped fonts.
findings.risk: None measurable — the guard is unreachable on all current fonts. Re-run pairsheet CLI on the 3 fonts to confirm identical summaries.

findings.title: join_scan and pairsheet agree where they overlap, but each covers link classes the other cannot; keep both until PS-1 lands, then pairsheet dominates
findings.evidence: Full-budget comparison (exp5): plain lowercase pairs — identical verdicts on all 3 fonts (both flag exactly 'dd' -> Dleftring->dflourishrightring on flourish, gap 0.87u; 0 elsewhere). Coverage differences measured: (a) join_scan words are <=3 chars so it can NEVER test medial->medial — the known ADda break (D->d, 1.72u) is caught only by pairsheet's midcaplower; (b) join_scan is lowercase-only (nameplate_fontcheck.py:389) — caplower/caps joins never scanned; (c) its 10 fixed contexts (line 365) cover 10 of 52 initial forms — it misses 'dda' (PS-1) too; (d) pairsheet misses initial->medial/medial->final (PS-1). Both use the same shape()/filled()/intersects pipeline so they cannot disagree on a shared measurement — confirmed empirically. Timing: full join_scan 7436 combos = 1.7/2.1/4.6 s; the check_font default budget of 6 s (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1287) completes all combos on this machine but has only 1.3x headroom on flourish — truncation on a slower machine is reported as a NOTE ('join-scan-partial'), not silent.
findings.proposed_fix: No behavioural change required for accuracy today. After PS-1: pairsheet's groups strictly subsume join_scan's lowercase coverage plus capitals; the clean long-term move is for check_font's letter-gaps finding to consume analyse_pairs results (PairResult.context supplies the example string junction_details needs) so one measuring system exists — do it additively (new code path with the old one as fallback) and keep the Finding/junction_details prompt pipeline byte-compatible. Until then, document in both modules which link classes each covers.
findings.accuracy_effect: None immediate (verdicts already agree). Delegation removes the risk of future divergence between two parallel geometry judges.
findings.risk: The delegation refactor touches the repair-prompt pipeline (_junctions_for, junction_details) that Sean pastes to font editors — regression-test the prompt text on the flourish font ('dd' junction must still name Dleftring/dflourishrightring with the same coordinates). GUI selftest asserts prompt properties (ASCII etc.).

findings.title: A tangent 'kiss' join passes both systems; weakest shipped join is already below the repair standard the tool itself demands
findings.evidence: OK requires only a.intersects(b) (nameplate_pairsheet.py:340, fontcheck name_gaps:155). claude_prompt tells the font editor a joint must overlap by >=1% of the em (~line 932: 'A hairline touch is NOT enough'), and overlap_margin uses 1.5% em (fontcheck:240-257), yet detection never measures overlap quality. Sweep of intersection areas over all passing mid+lower joins (exp7): TGCarrieSOFlourish 'Ny' mid join overlap area = 360 font-units^2, BELOW the (1% em)^2 = 419 u^2 square the repair prompt asks for; next weakest 'Yk' 570, 'yk' 758. Merriweather min 1623 u^2, TGCarrieSO min 1199 u^2. So the tool ships joins it would order fixed if they were 2 units further apart, and a genuine point-tangency (union pinch of zero width, which the laser severs) would pass silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Additive field on PairResult (e.g. overlap: float|None = None, default None so nothing positional changes) filled with the intersection area (or min junction width) for OK pairs in _test_pair/_test_middle; new WEAK amber tier in _cell_label and PairGrid when overlap < (0.01*upem)**2. Keep status OK so no existing verdict, count, or prompt changes unless the caller opts in. Measured cost: one .intersection() per OK pair, ~2 s extra per font on the full sweep — inside the 30 s budget.
findings.accuracy_effect: Surfaces physically fragile joins (pinch joints) that currently read as solid green; aligns detection with the tool's own repair criterion. No existing pass/fail flips.
findings.risk: New amber cells on fonts previously reported clean could read as a regression to Sean — present as 'weak join, eyeball it', not a failure. Verify pairsheet CLI exit code unchanged (only GAP/EMPTY/ERROR drive it).

findings.title: Generate-prompts section 2 hides the untested count when nothing failed
findings.evidence: nameplate_gui.py:3045-3054: after analyse_pairs (default 30 s budget), the note is 'Every letter pair that was tested joins cleanly.' when bad==0, with no mention of prep.n_untested; the body (which would carry claude_prompt's 'WARNING: N pairs were NOT tested') is only built when bad>0. A budget-starved run on a slow font would therefore produce a clean-sounding section. Latent today (full sweep max 3.0 s), same root as PS-2.
findings.proposed_fix: In the bad==0 branch at nameplate_gui.py:3052-3054, append f' ({prep.n_untested} pairs not reached in the time budget — unknown, not passes.)' when prep.budget_hit. Two lines, GUI-only.
findings.accuracy_effect: Keeps the 'not looked' vs 'passed' distinction in the prompts dialog, matching the CLI and PNG behaviour.
findings.risk: None; string-only change. GUI selftest checks prompt sections are ASCII/non-empty — keep the addition ASCII.

strengths: Cluster-span logic in _test_middle is CORRECT on the shipped fonts: all 4056 wrap words (2 mid groups x 676 x 3 fonts) shape to exactly 4 glyphs, one per character, clusters monotone 0..3 — no ligature ever crosses the wrapper boundary, so the (1,2) cluster window always isolates the true middle pair (exp1, zero anomalies).

Middle-link verdicts match whole-word union ground truth 4056/4056: 4055 OK pairs are connected in the full 'A..a' word, the single GAP (midcaplower Dd, 'ADda', 1.72u = 0.00084 em) is genuinely disconnected — the known ADda failure is caught with the right glyphs (D->d) named. Wrapper ink never bridges or masks a middle gap on any pair of any shipped font, and no GAP verdict's middle-span union was actually one piece, so judging only consecutive-glyph adjacency is empirically exact here (exp2).

pairsheet and join_scan never disagree where they measure the same thing: identical failing sets on the plain lowercase pairs of all 3 fonts (only 'dd' on TGCarrieSOFlourish, junction Dleftring->dflourishrightring, both systems), as expected since both ride nameplate_core.shape + Font.filled + shapely intersects (exp5).

The UNTESTED contract holds in the analyser: a starved run (budget 0.4 s) reported 3252 UNTESTED and 0 fake passes; MISSING is decided before the budget check so cmap holes are never mislabelled untested; EMPTY is a defect, not a pass (nameplate_pairsheet.py:489-508).

Budget is comfortable for the shipped fonts: full 5-group sweep (3380 cells) = 0.8 s (Merriweather), 1.0 s (TGCarrieSO), 3.0 s (TGCarrieSOFlourish) against the 30 s default — 10x headroom; the GUI's no-budget calls test everything today. Full join_scan (7436 combos) = 1.7/2.1/4.6 s.

The CLI summary and the PNG contact sheets surface UNTESTED correctly (amber 'UNTESTED' cell label, 'BUDGET RAN OUT — untested pairs are unknown, not passes' line); claude_prompt refuses to declare a font clean when budget_hit and repeats the warning in the failing case.

Positional-alternate sampling loses nothing on current fonts: deep-position (plain->plain) medial pairs at word positions 2-3 all join (0 gaps, both TG fonts, exp4); the .engN cut outlines are identical to their base glyph for every letter except the y/yflourish .eng3 family, whose links also pass; Merriweather's positional forms are position-independent so its 5-group coverage is complete (0 novel glyph pairs at the untested link classes).

PairGrid indexing is group-aware ((group,left,right) key, nameplate_gui.py:1214-1229), so identical char pairs in start vs middle groups are kept separate; the two-scale cell layout, per-glyph even-odd fill (counters stay open, overlaps stay black), and outline-only painting (no text API) are all correctly reasoned and implemented for the accuracy job the sheet does.

findings.title: brief() cap-height judge measures bbox height of a shaped single-letter 'H' - permanently NOT MET on most script/eyelet fonts, so the fix loop can never converge to exit 0
findings.evidence: nameplate_brief.py:371-388 builds the one-letter name 'H' and judges (y1-y0)*scale against the asked cap with tol 0.2%. A single-letter name shapes to a contextual variant whose ink leaves the [0, cap] band. Measured: Cervanttis-ExtraBoldEyelet 'H' shapes to H.eyeLR, ink -457.6..1169.1 fu vs cap reference 1444.17 fu, bbox 1.1264 in vs asked 1.000 -> NOT MET. Sweep of 8 real fonts: TGCarrieSO-v2 / TGCarrieSOFlourish-v2 / MerriweatherCut3Black = 1.0000 MET; Cervanttis-MediumEyelet 1.1195, ShineOnScriptMNB-Bold_2 1.0667, ShineOnScript2 1.0245, ShineOnSignature1-Regular 1.1162, Cervanttis-ExtraBoldEyelet 1.1264 = NOT MET. ShineOnScript2 and ShineOnSignature1 are FINISHED ground-truth corpus fonts, yet brief exits 1 on them forever (verdict path nameplate_brief.py:400-407 counts judge.failed). No edit can fix it inside the fences: the ink outside the band is the eyelet ring / swash, which the skills forbid touching.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_brief.py brief(), cap_height_check block (lines 371-388): stop judging bbox height. Judge the cap line instead: read the plain 'H' glyph's ink top in font units (font.cmap/contours, same technique as nameplate_core._cap_reference) and compare it with CORE._cap_reference(font)[0]; when they agree within ~2%, judge y-top of the flat capital (not y1-y0) against the asked cap; when H is not a flat-topped plain capital in this font (top differs from the reference, or the shaped form carries ink below baseline), emit the row as 'not judged - H is not a flat-topped capital in this font; cap line taken from the font's own flat capitals' and keep flat_top_capital_H as information only. Verdict then no longer counts an unmeetable row.
findings.accuracy_effect: Removes a permanently-false NOT MET that (a) blocks exit-0 convergence on 5 of 8 real fonts tested including two finished corpus fonts, and (b) pressures the editing Claude/worker to flatten the H swash or shrink letters - exactly the forbidden 'fix' per cap-height doctrine (flat caps exact, overshoot by design).
findings.risk: No golden risk: acceptance_tests/export_tests/regression_tests import only nameplate_layout/leadin/export (verified by grep) - nothing tests brief. Core untouched. Verify: brief on TGCarrieSO-v2 still READY/exit 0; on ShineOnScript2 the cap row becomes not-judged/MET; GUI selftest (51 checks) still passes since it never reads cap_height_check.

findings.title: Untested letter pairs are invisible to brief's verdict, exit code and JSON - exit 0 'READY' proven with 0.05 s pair budget
findings.evidence: Ran nameplate_brief.py --font fonts/TGCarrieSO-v2.otf --pair-budget 0.05 --min-thickness 0.06: verdict 'ready', EXITCODE=0, pairs JSON keys = ['flagged','worst_first'] only - no untested count, no budget_hit, though nearly all 3380 combos were UNTESTED. nameplate_pairsheet.py itself is scrupulous (UNTESTED is never a pass, PairReport.n_untested/budget_hit exist, claude_prompt warns), but nameplate_brief.py:218-243 only counts cells with .problem, and prompts['letter_pairs'] = '' whenever flagged==0, dropping even the prompt's own untested warning. The skills treat exit 0 as the only 'done', so an agent would declare an unmeasured font finished.
findings.proposed_fix: nameplate_brief.py brief(): after analyse_pairs, record prep.n_untested, prep.n_tested, prep.budget_hit into out['pairs']; when budget_hit, add a blocking-style line (e.g. out.setdefault('blocking',...).append(f'{n_untested} letter pairs were never tested - raise --pair-budget')) or at minimum force verdict 'needs work'; markdown(): print the untested count in the Letter pairs section instead of 'Every pair that was tested joins cleanly.' alone.
findings.accuracy_effect: Closes the one path where the convergence gate reports done without having measured; exit codes become trustworthy for the agent loop.
findings.risk: Fonts run with too-small budgets flip from ready to needs-work - the intended behavior. Default budget is safe (all 3380 Cervanttis combos tested inside the 30 s default; whole brief took 8.9 s). No test suite imports brief; GUI unaffected (it calls pairsheet directly).

findings.title: The four prompts contradict each other when used as the batch that brief.md / PromptsDialog present: fences forbid sibling tasks, two different overlap standards for the same junction, duplicated work orders, and only one of four asks for a versioned file back
findings.evidence: (a) Fence vs task: font_defects DO NOT CHANGE says 'the eyelet holes and their diameters... that hole keeps its size and position' (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1038-1040); thin_areas says 'Do not resize, move or reshape any eyelet hole' (nameplate_thickness.py:1095-1099); eyelet_size in the SAME brief.md says 'Resize the eyelet hole and the ring around it' (nameplate_eyelets.py:442-445). Pasted in sequence, each prompt's fence forbids the next prompt's work; pasted in reverse, prompt 1 instructs undoing prompt 4. (b) Margin mismatch: fontcheck overlap_margin = 1.5% em with a 4-kerf floor = 23 fu at the Cervanttis scale (nameplate_fontcheck.py:240-257); pairsheet uses max(8, 1% em) = 10 fu (nameplate_pairsheet.py:931-932). Same junction a.eyeL->j in one brief.json: fontcheck demands 64.7 fu travel / 23 fu overlap, pairsheet 'extend by >= 52 units' (41.7+10) - satisfying prompt 2 leaves under half of prompt 1's margin. (c) Duplication: the same a.eyeL exit stroke is item 2(a) of font_defects AND four rows of letter_pairs; fontcheck groups junctions internally precisely to prevent double-extension (module comment at _group_junctions), but nothing spans prompts. (d) Send-back: only fontcheck requests a version-suffixed filename (meta next_name, nameplate_fontcheck.py:1250) and a per-glyph change list; pairsheet/thickness/eyelet prompts have neither, so a repaired font can come back under the original name - the exact failure _next_filename's docstring names.
findings.proposed_fix: 1) Unify the margin: nameplate_pairsheet.claude_prompt gains optional scale=None and computes overlap via nameplate_fontcheck.overlap_margin(upem, scale); nameplate_brief.py and nameplate_gui.generate_prompts pass doc.scale when a doc exists. 2) Shared send-back: import _next_filename from fontcheck in pairsheet/thickness/eyelets claude_prompt and append 'Name the returned file <next> so it cannot be confused with <base>. List what you changed per glyph (name, glyph ID, points, before/after in font units).' 3) Sequencing contract: nameplate_brief.markdown() Prompts header and PromptsDialog head label add: 'Paste ONE block per round; when the font comes back, re-run and use the fresh blocks - these were all measured on the same version and the other blocks go stale the moment one is executed. The blocks overlap: junction fixes appear in both 1 and 2, and block 4 is the only one allowed to resize eyelets.' 4) In brief(), when prompts['eyelet_size'] is non-empty, append one line to font_defects and thin_areas: 'EXCEPTION: a separate eyelet-size request from this same report resizes the eyelet holes; that request wins for those holes.'
findings.accuracy_effect: Removes instructions that cancel each other across rounds, one 2.3x-inconsistent numeric requirement, and the double-extension path; every round returns a distinctly named file, which is the only state carrier the chat cycle has.
findings.risk: Text-only; no goldens involved. GUI selftest 9b6 assertions (4 sections, clean font blank, ASCII, eyelet contains 'FONT UNITS') must still pass - keep added text ASCII. Raising pairsheet's number from 10 to >=15/23 fu asks for slightly deeper overlaps: strictly safer for cutting, no checker gets stricter (pass condition is still intersection).

findings.title: No round-two memory: a defect that survives an edit round is re-asked verbatim with no 'this was asked before and did not move' signal
findings.evidence: State between rounds lives only in the font file. Verified the good parts: every prompt names the current file, re-measures, and lists only current defects. But nothing compares rounds: check_font (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1286+) takes only a path; brief() has no --prev; the filename is the only carrier and _next_filename degrades to '-fixed-fixed' after round 1 on unversioned names (proven: 'MyFont-fixed.ttf' -> 'MyFont-fixed-fixed.ttf'), while pairsheet/thickness/eyelet prompts carry no version request at all. If the same junction gap measures 41.7 fu in round 1 and 41.7 fu in round 2, the round-2 prompt is byte-identical in substance and the receiving Claude (fresh chat, no history) repeats the same failed edit.
findings.proposed_fix: Two additive pieces. (1) nameplate_fontcheck.check_font: when re.search(r'(?:-v(\d+)|-fixed(?:-fixed)*)$' matches the stem, set rep.meta['round_note'] and have _prompt_body print after the header: 'The file name says this font has been repaired at least once. If a defect below matches one from an earlier request, the previous edit did not move the number - first say why, then fix it differently; do not repeat the same edit.' (2) nameplate_brief.py: add --prev-json; when given, diff targets[] and pairs.worst_first / font_check findings by stable keys (junction glyph-pair string, target name), annotate each unchanged row with 'UNCHANGED since <prev file>' in targets_text, markdown, and prepend a STALLED list to the affected prompt blocks. The measured numbers are already embedded in every prompt, so the delta becomes visible the moment two rounds are compared.
findings.accuracy_effect: Turns silent non-convergence (the circular cycle's worst failure mode) into an explicit signal the next editor and Sean both see; no measurement changes.
findings.risk: Additive CLI flag and prompt lines; nothing golden. Keep the note ASCII for the selftest. False positive possible if Sean renames files arbitrarily - the note is worded as a hint, not an accusation.

findings.title: Thickness prompt violates its own paste contracts: em dashes break the ASCII rule (selftest hole proven) and the verification command is unquoted, so it is broken for any font path with spaces
findings.evidence: Generated brief.json for Cervanttis: prompts.thin_areas contains U+2014 (verified by scanning the JSON; the other three blocks are clean ASCII). Sources: nameplate_thickness.py:992 ('FONT THICKENING REQUEST — ShineOn...'), :1031-1032 ('...font units — round up to...'), :1045 ('{who} — {sp.where} of the letter'). The GUI selftest asserts 'every prompt is plain ASCII' (nameplate_gui.py:3669-3671) but passes only because thin_spin is reset to 0.0 at nameplate_gui.py:3508 before step 9b6, so the thin body is empty - the check misses exactly the block that violates it. Separately, nameplate_thickness.py:1117 emits the check command with an unquoted filename: 'python nameplate_thickness.py Cervanttis-ExtraBoldEyelet (1).ttf "ADAM" 1 in cap 0.1' - unrunnable as printed; several real fonts have spaces ('TG CARRIE_SO.otf').
findings.proposed_fix: nameplate_thickness.claude_prompt_from_spots: replace the three em dashes with '-' (or run header/item lines through an ASCII flatten like nameplate_fontcheck._plain); quote the filename in the HOW IT WILL BE CHECKED line (f'"{fname}"'). Optionally strengthen the selftest: set win.thin_spin to a value that yields a non-empty body before step 9b6 so the ASCII assertion covers a real thickness prompt.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on measurements; restores the stated 'pastes anywhere' contract and makes the printed pass/fail re-check command actually runnable, which is part of the convergence loop.
findings.risk: None - text only. GUI selftest must still pass; the em-dash fix is what makes its ASCII assertion true rather than vacuous.

findings.title: Eyelet prompt is the least self-contained of the four: no unitsPerEm, no glyph names/IDs (unactionable on post-3.0 fonts), no verification command, no send-back
findings.evidence: Generated eyelet block for Cervanttis (nameplate_eyelets.claude_prompt, lines 392-457): states file+family, physical and font-unit targets, but never states unitsPerEm (both sibling join prompts call it essential); names zero glyphs - 'change it in EVERY glyph that carries one' is the exact vagueness the audit question flags, and in a post-3.0 font (TGCarrie: no glyph names at all, per fontcheck's own NOTE) an editor cannot even search by the .eye naming convention; no HOW IT WILL BE CHECKED; no versioned-filename/change-list request. Enumerating the carrying glyphs is trivially cheap: shaping c+'aa' and 'aa'+c for all 52 letters collected 104 first/last contextual forms with glyph IDs in 1 ms on Cervanttis (A.eyeL gid 123, A.eyeR gid 124, ...).
findings.proposed_fix: nameplate_eyelets.claude_prompt(doc, ..., font=None): accept the Font (nameplate_brief.py:313 and nameplate_gui.py:3094 both already hold one - pass it through). Print 'unitsPerEm <upem>; 1 font unit = <doc.scale> <unit> at this size'. Probe shape(font, c+'aa') and shape(font, 'aa'+c) for every cmapped letter, collect placed[0]/placed[-1] glyphs that differ from the base cmap glyph, and list them with glyph IDs as 'THE GLYPHS THAT CARRY AN EYELET - change all of them, and only the eyelet ring in them'. Append 'HOW IT WILL BE CHECKED: python nameplate_eyelets.py "<font>" "<name>" <h> <unit> <basis> <id> <wall>' and the shared send-back/next-name block (PR-3).
findings.accuracy_effect: Makes the eyelet instruction executable without opening the app and prevents the known failure of fixing only the glyphs the test name happened to use (ends stop matching); adds the missing sanity anchor (upem) that the other prompts treat as mandatory.
findings.risk: Keep the font parameter optional so the prompt still renders with font=None. GUI selftest asserts 'FONT UNITS' appears in the eyelet body - additions preserve it. Probe cost ~1 ms measured; no goldens.

findings.title: Pairsheet prompt scales badly (75.8k chars, one line per 538 pairs) and its group design never tests the first/last junctions of 3+-letter words, so its 'how it will be checked' overstates coverage
findings.evidence: Cervanttis prompts.letter_pairs = 75,756 chars (measured) - one 2-line entry per failing pair even though by_left() already buckets them and fontcheck compresses the same defect class from 354 junctions to 7 edits in 31k chars. Coverage: GROUP_SPECS (nameplate_pairsheet.py:90-104) has only 'start' (the pair IS the whole 2-letter word, so BOTH letters take eye forms) and 'middle' (A...a wrap, both medial). eyeL->medial and medial->eyeR junctions - the first and last junctions of every real 3+-letter name - are shaped by neither: fontcheck's list contains a.eyeL->j (from 'aja') while pairsheet's 'a' bucket has only a.eyeL->j.eyeR (from 'aj'). Those junctions are covered today only by fontcheck's separate budget-bounded join_scan.
findings.proposed_fix: Prompt side (safe, text-only): in nameplate_pairsheet.claude_prompt, emit one work item per left glyph using the existing by_left() buckets - lead with the worst gap and shaped left-glyph name, then a compact 'also fails against: o (8.2), t (8.1), z (7.5)' line - and state explicitly that the sweep tests whole-2-letter words and wrapped middles, with first/last-of-longer-word junctions verified by the font-defects scan. Coverage side (larger, optional): add 'first' / 'last' group modes (shape pair+'aa' and 'aa'+pair, judge only the link between clusters 0-1 resp. 2-3, reusing _test_middle's cluster machinery); note GROUP_KEYS feeds the GUI grid, so that change needs the GUI selftest re-run.
findings.accuracy_effect: A prompt a chat model can actually hold and act on (an editor asked for ~40 grouped stroke edits converges; one asked for 538 individual extends does not), and honest coverage claims; the optional new modes close a real measurement blind spot.
findings.risk: Prompt rewrite: none (no suite reads it; keep ASCII). New group modes: touches analyse_pairs/GUI grid - do separately and re-run the 51-check selftest and a manual pairsheet render.

findings.title: GLYPHS IN SCOPE count contradicts itself when the un-measured junction list is non-empty, and the send-back checksum enforces the wrong number
findings.evidence: Cervanttis font_defects block: 'GLYPHS IN SCOPE - 4 existing glyph(s), and no others' followed immediately by 'Also in scope: ... the left-hand glyph of each junction in the un-measured list above' - which names ~50 more glyphs via item 2(g). Send-back item 5 (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1270-1273) tells the editor the edited-glyph count must 'match ... the GLYPHS IN SCOPE count above', so an editor who legitimately fixes the un-measured junctions fails the prompt's own checksum. Sources: _scope_glyphs only harvests measured junction data (nameplate_fontcheck.py:973-997); header at 1203-1204.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_fontcheck._prompt_body: derive the extra left-glyph names from the 'extra' data (junction string split on '->', left half; they are stated in the list already) and print 'GLYPHS IN SCOPE - 4 named below, plus up to N more: the left-hand glyphs of the un-measured junction list in item 2'; reword send-back item 5 to 'matches that list plus any left-hand glyphs from the un-measured list you fixed - name each one'.
findings.accuracy_effect: Removes a self-contradiction that either deters legitimate fixes or trains the editor to ignore the checksum - the checksum is the cheapest collateral-damage detector the cycle has.
findings.risk: None; prompt text only. Keep ASCII; no suites read this text.

findings.title: brief() judges only the LEFT eyelet: exit 0 is possible with the right eyelet off target
findings.evidence: nameplate_brief.py:303-312: 'e = eyes[0]' and both judge.add calls use only it; measure_eyelets returns up to 2 eyelets sorted left-to-right and both are reported and prompted, but only the left one gates the verdict. An edit that fixes only the .eyeL family (a plausible partial edit, since the prompt lists LEFT first) reaches exit 0 with the right eyelet still wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Judge the worst of both: for inner diameter use the eyelet whose |measured-target| is largest; for wall use min(wall) across eyelets; label the rows 'eyelet inner diameter (worst end)' so the text stays truthful. Pure addition in brief(); prompts already cover both ends.
findings.accuracy_effect: The convergence gate stops passing half-fixed eyelets; symmetric-by-construction fonts (like Cervanttis, both ends 0.0623) are unaffected.
findings.risk: Verdicts can only get stricter; no suites cover brief. Verify with a brief run on TGCarrie (targets judged on both ends, still consistent).

findings.title: _next_filename degenerates to '-fixed-fixed' from round 2 on unversioned names
findings.evidence: Verified: 'MyFont.ttf' -> 'MyFont-fixed.ttf' -> 'MyFont-fixed-fixed.ttf'; 'Cervanttis-ExtraBoldEyelet (1).ttf' follows the same path. Versioned names work correctly ('TGCarrieSO-v2.otf' -> 'TGCarrieSO-v3.otf', case-insensitive 'Font-V9' -> 'Font-V10'). No overwrite ever happens (names stay unique), but the round number - the only cross-round state the chat cycle has (PR-4) - is lost after round 1.
findings.proposed_fix: nameplate_fontcheck._next_filename: before the '-fixed' fallback, match r'-fixed(\d*)$' and emit '-fixed2', '-fixed3', ...; or better, emit '-v2' for the first repair so every subsequent round rides the existing vN+1 path.
findings.accuracy_effect: Keeps a monotonic round counter in the filename, which PR-4's round-awareness note depends on; prevents absurd names that invite Sean to rename by hand (and lose the counter).
findings.risk: None; the function is only used to compose prompt text. Add the two cases to a quick python -c check as done in this audit.

strengths: nameplate_fontcheck.Report.claude_prompt() is exemplary as a self-contained work order, verified on a real defective font (Cervanttis): file, family (name ID 4), unitsPerEm, outline container, post-3.0 no-names warning with glyph-ID discipline, the shaping feature list that picked the alternates, and the measurement basis with the fu<->inch conversion stated in both directions plus the exact historical failure mode ('an inch number treated as a font-unit number is ~1444x too small').

fontcheck junction instructions carry coordinates in the edited glyph's own frame, disambiguate contextual alternates from base glyphs with both glyph IDs ('Edit A.eyeL. Leave A alone.'), group same-stroke junctions (354 junctions -> 7 edits, preventing four 30-unit extensions of one stroke becoming 120), warn when a gap is wider than a stroke (19% of em -> 'the connector is missing rather than short'), and offer the narrower right-side edit with 'one side or the other, never both'.

Numeric cross-consistency holds across the whole prompt set: 193.5 fu <-> 0.134 in and 59.3 fu <-> 0.0411 in both match measured_on.units_per_in exactly; the eyelet targets are internally consistent (541.6 + 2x288.8 = 1119.2); the sub-kerf floor and margins are restated in font units, never inches, wherever the editor works.

The DO-NOT-CHANGE fence is built from the report, not fixed, so it never contradicts its own tasks: with bad-upem present the unitsPerEm bullet is dropped; with missing letters the glyph-order bullet gains the append-at-end exception; COLR bullets appear only when layers exist and are correct.

Convergence basics (a)-(c) all hold: every round's prompts name the current file, re-measure everything from it, and list only current defects - verified on two clean fonts (TGCarrieSO-v2, AlwaysInMyHeart-v22 produce explicit 'No repair needed... do not modify' with notes fenced as background) and one defective font.

fontcheck's next_name mechanic works for versioned names ('TGCarrieSO-v2.otf' -> 'TGCarrieSO-v3.otf', case-insensitive) and its dead-file path refuses to print a work order around a font that could not be opened - no invented unitsPerEm, no invented tables.

brief.json prompts and the GUI PromptsDialog call the SAME four generator functions (rep.claude_prompt / PS.claude_prompt / TH.claude_prompt / EY.claude_prompt) - there is no forked prompt text; the two paths differ only in inputs (GUI: typed name, GUI height/unit/basis, spinbox targets; brief: test names + CLI targets), which is by design.

Empty-prompt semantics ('empty block = nothing to fix; do not invent work') are implemented consistently in brief(), markdown(), PromptsDialog (blank box with placeholder), and are correctly documented in both consumer skills (nameplate-font and font-production SKILL.md).

nameplate_thickness refuses to emit font-unit numbers for stacked sheets rather than print sizes wrong by three orders of magnitude, and refuses missing/zero/negative targets in words; nameplate_eyelets._valid_target likewise rejects 0/negative targets loudly instead of silently dropping them.

nameplate_pairsheet's own honesty rules are sound: UNTESTED/MISSING are never passes in its report or prompt, the budget warning appears whenever failures exist, and the prompt explains kern-pushed gaps must be closed by drawing, not re-kerning (the defect is only in how brief consumes it - finding PR-2).

Failure containment around the prompts is good: _build_prompt falls back to a plain restatement rather than losing findings, Finding.instruction() falls back to prose that admits it could not measure, _plain() flattens typography while deliberately preserving family and glyph names, and _emit() survives cp1252 consoles.

findings.title: survey() misses the true thinnest material on all three shipped-font test names — worst case reports 6.6x thicker than reality (golden-file verified)
findings.evidence: Uniform edge-midpoint sampling (nameplate_thickness.py:175-207 _walk, :81 MAX_SAMPLES=900) casts only along segment normals, so a minimal chord that terminates at a boundary VERTEX (notch tip, counter apex) has a near-zero acceptance window and is structurally invisible at any density. Measured with a vertex-anchored probe that reuses the module's own _cross_width semantics (wedge test included), then independently verified with a 360-direction fan probe (minimal chord through midpoint) and against the shipped golden artifact: (a) ADAM @1in cap, Merriweather Cut3: survey@900 thinnest=0.08493in (126.20fu); true accepted minimum = 72.76fu = 0.04896in, a web between an engrave-notch tip (2151.1,130.9) and the D's outer curve (2091.5,89.1); fan probe 73.04fu, clearance 36.38 = 0.4997*d (genuine parallel-wall web). Golden/ADAM_cap1in.svg's own CUT polygon measures 0.04929in at that spot while the module says 0.08493 — +73% over-report. Denser sampling never converges: 28800 samples (3.5s) still reads 0.07961in (+62% vs truth). (b) CHRISTOPHER @1in: survey@900 = 0.08082in (120.09fu); true web between two nearly-meeting V-notch tips at x=1081.0 is 18.13fu = 0.0122in (fan probe 18.13, clearance 9.05=d/2) — report is 6.6x the truth; that web WILL snap. (c) Carrie (TGCarrieSO) @25mm: survey@900 = 98.12fu; true 79.4-80.6fu (+22% over-report). Secondary mechanism, same root cause: vertex-to-EDGE minima converge only O(1/N) — ADAM's M counter-apex web (true 117.0fu, from boundary dump 1486.0-1369.0) reads 126.20 at 900 (+7.9%), needs 14400 samples (1.8s) for +1.1%, est. ~140k samples (~18s) for <1%. Boundary spacing at 900: ADAM 0.98mm/sample (692 places over 26.78in perimeter), CHRISTOPHER 1.69mm/sample. Bias is one-directional: no false-thin reading was observed in any experiment — the tool only errs thick or misses.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_thickness.py only (additive, core untouched): add a vertex-anchored probe pass inside survey() after the uniform walk — for every material-ring vertex v, STRtree-query boundary segments within a ceiling (e.g. 1.2x the uniform-walk thinnest, or 1.5x target when given), take the foot q of the perpendicular from v on each candidate, call the existing _cross_width(solid, q, normal-toward-v, reach), and feed accepted readings into the same raw pool so clustering/attribution/notes work unchanged. Prototype accuracy: ADAM -0.1%, CHRISTOPHER +0.0%, Carrie +1.5% vs truth; also fixes the synthetic V-pinch (8.00fu exact where current code returns 'no thin spot'). Naive prototype cost +4.2s (ADAM) to +36s (Carrie) on top of 0.15-0.27s; still under the 1-min usability bar, and large engineering headroom remains (reflex-vertex filter with signed-area orientation, direction pre-filter to skip outward candidates — a capped nearest-6 version ran 0.5-5s but needs that filter to not starve, vectorized shapely 2 contains, progressive best-first ceiling).
findings.accuracy_effect: Removes a +22% to +560% systematic over-report of minimum thickness on the shipped fonts. Concrete misjudgment eliminated: ADAM with any min-thickness target between 0.049 and 0.085in currently gets a false PASS; with the brief's example target 0.10in the required-increase figure is +17.8% when the truth is +104%, and claude_prompt's own verification loop (HOW IT WILL BE CHECKED) passes a font whose 0.049in web was never touched.
findings.risk: More and thinner spots appear in reports, GUI badge (nameplate_gui.py:486), brief JSON, and claude_prompt — that is the intended behavior change, but any snapshot-style expectations on report text would shift. nameplate_core.py and nameplate_export.py untouched, so acceptance_tests.py (53) golden SVGs and export_tests.py (31) cut-order contract cannot break by construction — still rerun all four suites (acceptance, export, regression, GUI selftest 51) plus a before/after timing check that a survey stays <1min on the longest supported name.

findings.title: Wedge test (STRAIGHTNESS=0.42) is fully blind to straight-walled V-pinch waists past ~33 deg convergence and biases tapered stroke-ends thick by ~1% per degree
findings.evidence: Synthetic sweep (waist 8fu, 3600 samples): total wall convergence 10deg -> +1.6%, 20deg -> +5.9%, 30deg -> +13.4%, 33/36/40/45/60deg -> ZERO readings anywhere on the shape ('Nothing in this artwork reads as a thin stroke') because every crossing fails room >= 0.42*d (nameplate_thickness.py:93, :250-251). A waist between converging straight walls is not the serif-tip case the rejection was written for. Flat-tipped tapers read thick at the end: the last 0.42*w of any stroke end is unmeasurable, giving +1.2% at 1.6deg convergence, +5.3% at 6.5deg, +21.1% at 21deg (tip width 40fu). Counter-evidence bounding the blast radius: smooth circular-arc pinches measure to within +0.41% even at wall radius 6fu, and no straight-walled V-pinch was found on the three shipped fonts — currently a latent risk for future calligraphic/brush fonts rather than a live defect.
findings.proposed_fix: The TH-1 vertex probe already cures the waist case within existing semantics (V-pinch waist vertices are reflex; probe returned 8.00fu exact at 45deg where survey() returns nothing) — no STRAIGHTNESS change needed. Optionally document in the module header that straight-walled waists steeper than ~33deg are invisible to the uniform walk alone, and keep the taper-end exclusion as-is (it is the documented intentional wedge semantics, bounded and biased only near stroke ends).
findings.accuracy_effect: With the TH-1 probe: worst-case 'invisible waist' class goes from unbounded error (reported as no-thin-spot) to exact. Without it: a steeply-pinched script join would silently pass any target.
findings.risk: None beyond TH-1's risk if fixed via the probe. Lowering STRAIGHTNESS instead would be the wrong fix — it would admit true wedge tips as false thin spots; keep 0.42.

findings.title: _regions merges two distinct thin features into one spot when they sit within 1.6x thickness across empty space
findings.evidence: Clustering (nameplate_thickness.py:531-574) links samples by Euclidean distance (radius = max(LINK_T*t0, LINK_S*spacing)) with no material-connectivity check. Synthetic comb, two 20fu-wide arms: gap 150fu -> 8 spots at 20fu (each 300fu arm correctly splits into ~4 span-limited rows, both arms visible); gap 60fu -> same; gap 30fu (=1.5x thickness, within LINK_T=1.6) -> 4 spots with n_samples doubled (33->64): the two arms fused, the report names one position and the second distinct thin feature disappears as a separate row. Real-world exposure: double strokes / tight parallel thin walls closer than ~1.6x their own thickness.
findings.proposed_fix: In _regions (or its caller), accept a link between two samples only if the straight connector between their crossing midpoints stays in material (one prepared contains test on the connector midpoint is a cheap 90% proxy), falling back to the current rule when the geometry is unavailable. Pure nameplate_thickness.py change.
findings.accuracy_effect: Thinnest value unaffected (worst reading still reported); improves the COUNT and per-spot typical/extent/position honesty for tight double-stroke features, which n_below_target and the claude_prompt area list rely on.
findings.risk: Spot counts rise for tight geometry, so report text lines change; verify report-driven expectations in GUI selftest and any brief output checks. Slight extra cost per link test (bounded: pool <= ~350 samples).

findings.title: Brief JSON drops survey.n_areas / n_below_target, so consumers see at most top_n=8 below-target areas when 18-25 exist
findings.evidence: Measured at 900 samples with the brief's documented example target 0.10in: ADAM n_areas=28, n_below_target=18; CHRISTOPHER n_areas=56, n_below_target=25; survey returns 8 spots (top_n default, nameplate_thickness.py:577,731). report_text and claude_prompt handle this honestly ('18 of 28 distinct areas', '...and N more area(s) under the minimum, the instruction is a rule not a list'). But nameplate_brief.py:333-363 builds out['thickness'] with only the 8 spots and a 'below_target' list of ranks WITHIN those 8 — n_areas and n_below_target from the Survey are discarded, so an AI or human reading the brief JSON undercounts the problem by 2-3x. The pass/fail judge itself is safe (it uses spots[0], the worst).
findings.proposed_fix: Additive keys in nameplate_brief.py's thickness block: 'n_areas': surv.n_areas, 'n_below_target': surv.n_below_target (and optionally 'spots_truncated': surv.n_areas > len(spots)). For spot #9+ the existing claude_prompt rule-based instruction is the right treatment — no need to list more rows, just carry the counts.
findings.accuracy_effect: No measurement change; removes a 2-3x undercount of below-target areas for downstream consumers of the brief JSON.
findings.risk: New JSON keys only — verify nothing schema-validates the brief dict strictly; rerun the brief CLI and GUI selftest.

findings.title: n_areas is unstable across sampling density (ADAM: 28 areas at 900 samples, 12 at 28800) and one physical taper reports as 6 areas
findings.evidence: ADAM n_areas: 27@300, 28@900, 24@1800, 17@7200, 12@28800; CHRISTOPHER: 38@300, 56@900, 17@28800. Cause: the cluster pool is truncated to the thinnest POOL=300 samples (+4 per glyph) (nameplate_thickness.py:99-100, 643-650), so which samples exist to cluster changes with density; additionally MAX_SPAN_T/THICK_TOL deliberately split long gentle features — a single 8->30fu taper yields 6 areas at 900 samples. The 'N of M distinct areas' wording in report_text and claude_prompt presents this count as a stable fact.
findings.proposed_fix: Cheapest honest fix is wording: 'at least N distinct areas at this sampling' in report_text/claude_prompt_from_spots. A stabler count would need clustering on all below-1.5x-worst samples rather than a fixed 300-sample pool (bounded extra O(n^2) work since the pool stays small in practice).
findings.accuracy_effect: No thickness value changes; stops the area COUNT from silently varying with the samples argument (brief exposes --samples, nameplate_brief.py:548).
findings.risk: Text changes only; rerun GUI selftest and any output-comparing checks.

findings.title: Notch-tip webs get the generic 'thicken the stroke' instruction — no note that the engrave slit, not stroke weight, sets the thickness
findings.evidence: The two worst true webs found (ADAM D 72.8fu, CHRISTOPHER 18.1fu) are both bounded on one side by a V-notch tip cut into the letter (this font family realizes engraving detail as slits; boundary dumps show wedge-tip vertices at (2151.1,130.9) and (1081.0,395.0)/(1081.0,413.2)). The note machinery already special-cases eyelet walls and .notdef boxes (nameplate_thickness.py:689-718) precisely so the thickening instruction doesn't misdirect, but a notch-web spot would tell a font editor to 'move the INNER wall of the stroke' when the actionable fix is shortening/shallowing the notch. Only becomes user-visible once TH-1 lands (today these spots are never found).
findings.proposed_fix: When a spot's crossing endpoint lies within a few units of a boundary vertex whose interior angle is a deep V into material (data the TH-1 vertex probe already has), append a note: 'one wall of this reading is the tip of an engraved notch — shortening the notch is the likelier fix than thickening the stroke'. nameplate_thickness.py only.
findings.accuracy_effect: No measurement change; prevents a misdirected font edit for the newly-reportable class of spots.
findings.risk: Note text additions only; keep note priority order (notdef > eyelet > notch > lone-reading).

findings.title: Deferred-plan verdict: 'denser thin-area report sampling' does not fix accuracy — vertex-anchored probing does
findings.evidence: Densification measured: 32x the default budget (28800 samples, 3.5s vs 0.17s) still over-reports ADAM's true minimum by +62% (0.0796 vs 0.0490in) because vertex-terminated chords have ~zero acceptance window under normal-cast sampling; adaptive refinement around coarse-pass thin areas cannot help since the coarse pass records nothing at those locations (at 900 samples, zero readings exist within the M-top or D-web regions). Meanwhile the vertex probe at unchanged 900 uniform samples reaches -0.1% / +0.0% / +1.5% of truth on ADAM / CHRISTOPHER / Carrie and fixes the synthetic V-pinch and 2-blob-neck cases.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the deferred 'denser sampling' item with TH-1's vertex-anchored probe. Do not raise MAX_SAMPLES as an accuracy measure (it only helps vertex-to-EDGE minima, slowly: ADAM M-apex +7.9%@900 -> +1.1%@14400/1.8s). A modest bump (e.g. 900->1800, ~0.3-0.5s) is defensible purely to tighten edge-interior minima like Carrie@300's +15%, but it is second-order next to the probe.
findings.accuracy_effect: Adopting probe over densification: error on true minimum goes from +22%..+560% (unfixable by density) to <=1.5% on all three shipped-font names.
findings.risk: Same as TH-1. If instead only densification were adopted, accuracy would remain wrong at 32x the runtime — the worthless-upgrade case the prime rule warns about.

strengths: _cross_width is exact on parallel-wall geometry: synthetic rect 100x700 measured 100.00fu (0.000% err), L-arm 60.00 (0.000%), annulus wall 50.00 (-0.008%), all at the default 900 samples (0.1-0.2s).
Smooth curved pinches — the realistic script-join shape — measure to within +0.12% down to wall radius 25fu and +0.41% at radius 6fu: the wedge test does not harm curved-wall waists.

The across-direction choice at serif feet is correct: a thin slab reads its thin dimension (slab height), not its long dimension; grazing/cusp logic produced zero false-thin readings in every experiment — the tool's bias is strictly 'reads thick or misses', never a false alarm, so any below-target report it makes can be trusted.

Letter attribution is correct in every case inspected: Merriweather contextual glyphs (A.ini, A.e5, M.e0, D.e0) attributed to the right letters at the right positions; typed case honored ('Adam' reports 'm (M.e0)', not 'M') via the positional-corroboration path; TGCarrieSO is post format 3.0 but attribution still works because CFF charset names survive (Cleftring, erightring), and spot positions land inside the correct glyphs' x-ranges.

Sheet handling is honest by construction: _is_sheet gates letter attribution (preventing cross-name misattribution), report_text drops font-unit columns, and claude_prompt refuses to emit numbers that would be off by 1000x — all verified by code path reading.
The sampling budget is honored and honestly accounted: 900 requested -> 692-847 places on real names, samples_taken/samples_used printed in the report; survey runtime 0.15-0.27s at default.

report_text and claude_prompt handle the >top_n case honestly at the text level: '18 of 28 distinct areas are thinner... the 8 worst are listed', '...and N more area(s) under the minimum' plus a rule-based instruction that covers unlisted areas; the pass/fail judge in nameplate_brief uses the single worst spot, which is the correct statistic.

The eps/span tolerance derivation in _Solid (artwork-diagonal based, not em-based, never thickness-proportional) is sound for both font-unit and sheet frames, and the eyelet-wall note reuses nameplate_eyelets' own constants so the two tools cannot drift apart.

The lone-reading note ('a single reading with nothing beside it to corroborate') fired exactly where it should in testing — on the one-sample M-apex region at 28800 samples — and its wording is a fact about the row, not a hedge.

findings.title: Depth-2 islands are erased from the material mask, so lead-ins cut straight through nested parts (reachable by typing © or ® in both TGCarrie fonts)
findings.evidence: nameplate_leadin.py:157-161 builds material = unary_union(even-depth rings) - unary_union(odd-depth rings). A hole ring (depth 1) geometrically covers everything nested inside it, so subtracting it deletes any depth-2 island from the mask, and every safety check (_usable_length, _verify) then sees empty space where a solid part sits. Demonstrated two ways. (a) Synthetic plate/hole/island/counter doc (scratch patho_leadin.py): _analyse classifies depths [0,1,2,3] correctly, but material.contains(island body point) == False; lead_in_report then emits a lead from (665.7,340)->(665.7,440) that runs 0.1000 in straight THROUGH the island body, and the island-counter's lead exits the counter and cuts 0.0200 in of island wall. (b) Real, typeable glyphs (scratch depth_hits.py): '©' (U+00A9) and '®' (U+00AE) exist in the cmaps of both TGCarrieSO-v2.otf and TGCarrieSOFlourish-v2.otf and build depth-2/3 documents; shipped lead_in_report at GUI defaults (0.100 in lead, 0.012 in standoff) produces: '©' hole-ring-1 lead crossing 0.0128 in of the C island and outer lead crossing 0.0318 in; '®' outer lead crossing 0.0807 in of the R island, plus a hole lead passing 0.0038 in from it (< 0.004 in kerf floor). A cmap-wide scan (scratch depth_scan.py; 282/435/433 documents across the three fonts) shows these two characters are the ONLY reachable depth>=2 cases; MerriweatherCut3Black-Engrave-v2.ttf has none, and all 9 ADAM/Adam/OLIVIA docs are max_depth=1 (unaffected).
findings.proposed_fix: In _analyse() in C:/Users/Zack/Documents/Calude Code Apps/nameplate-app/nameplate_leadin.py, build the material by alternating in ascending depth order instead of one union-minus-union: mat = union(depth-0 polys); for d = 1,2,...: mat = mat.difference(union(depth-d)) if d is odd else mat.union(union(depth-d)). Same signature, same (polys, depths) returned; for max depth <= 1 the expression reduces to exactly the current union(depth0)-union(depth1), so every existing document's output is bit-identical. Purely internal — no core change, goldens untouched.
findings.accuracy_effect: Eliminates lead-ins that physically cut through (or graze inside kerf of) nested solid artwork — up to 0.0807 in of through-cut on '®' today. Zero change for every depth<=1 document, which is every existing test and all plain-name jobs.
findings.risk: Only documents containing depth>=2 rings change, and those are wrong today. Exposure is low (©/® on a nameplate is rare, and fontcheck would flag the loose island as not-connected anyway), but the module's own 'never through the material' guarantee is silently false for them. Prove no regression with acceptance_tests.py (53, incl. byte-identical goldens — which use svg_single without lead-ins), export_tests.py (31), regression_tests.py (12), GUI selftest (51), stress_test.py, then re-run scratch depth_hits.py and confirm 0 island violations.

findings.title: Adaptive lead-in sampling (deferred plan item): current sampler is already near-optimal on the shipped fonts, but forfeits standoff on tapered holes; a 3-line-of-concept adaptive variant fixes that at 1.18x runtime
findings.evidence: Measured, all at GUI defaults (1.0 in cap, 0.100 in lead, 0.012 in standoff). (1) Shipped vs exhaustive (512-1024 arc samples, no early break, same length-then-room criteria; scratch audit_leadin.py) over all 92 served leads of ADAM/Adam/OLIVIA x 3 fonts: mean pierce-room left on the table 0.00 mil, worst 0.2 mil (Carrie/Flour 'ADAM' ring 12); worst length left 1.4 mil; no skipped hole was servable at any ladder level; no hole could hold a higher standoff than shipped chose. The n_full>=8 early break (nameplate_leadin.py:348-352) therefore costs at most 0.2 mil of room on real fonts — a validated shortcut. (2) Pathological synthetics (scratch patho_leadin.py): straight and 30-degree slits (0.018 in), crescent, and pocket-in-slot all match exhaustive within 0.1 mil, and the per-segment sampling minimum in _candidates (nameplate_leadin.py:244) finds a 0.040 in pocket in a 0.012 in slot at full standoff. The failure case is a TAPERED hole: a 0.5 in wedge narrowing 0.030->0 in gets standoff 0.0078 in / length 0.0217 in from the shipped sampler when 0.0120 in / 0.0831 in genuinely fits (56-sample spacing 18.4 fu puts the wide end edge's 2 samples off the centerline, the full-standoff level finds nothing, and the ladder relaxes a step it did not need to). (3) Prototype 'proto2' (scratch proto2_leadin.py): keeps the shipped coarse pass AND early break, adds only (a) shrinking-window arc refinement (3 rounds x 6 points) of the best candidate when it is shorter than the requested length, and (b) one retry of the SAME ladder level at 4x density (224) before relaxing the standoff. Results: wedge served at full 0.0120 in standoff, length 0.0998 in; on the 9 real docs, identical standoffs and skips everywhere, +0.6..+1.3 mil more lead length on the 10 tight holes, runtime 2.39s -> 2.82s total (1.18x, worst single name ~+70 ms). A no-early-break variant with full refinement (scratch proto_leadin.py) costs 6.35x for <= 0.2 mil extra room — not worth it. (4) Safety: prototype outputs pass the full invariant harness (0 violations, see strengths) on all 9 docs and all synthetics; sub-kerf slit and tiny triangle still correctly skipped and reported.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement proto2's two additions inside nameplate_leadin.py, both additive: in _find_lead_in(), after the existing selection, locally refine the winner along its arc neighbourhood only when its usable length < requested length (new optional param, e.g. refine=True, default can be True since goldens contain no lead-ins and all lead-in tests are property-based); in lead_in_report()'s attempt(), retry a ladder level once with _candidates(ring, 4*_SAMPLES) before stepping down the clearance ladder. Reference implementation: scratch proto2_leadin.py (proto2_find / proto2_report).
findings.accuracy_effect: On shipped fonts: +0.6..+1.3 mil lead length on tight counters (Merri 'A' counter 0.0156->0.0169 in), standoffs unchanged — strictly better or equal. On tapered/pathological holes: prevents unnecessary standoff relaxation (wedge case pierce standoff +54%, 0.0078->0.0120 in). Never worse: selection criteria, ladder, floors and _verify are unchanged.
findings.risk: Lead pierce positions shift slightly on holes that do not fit the full length, so any workflow diffing exported SVGs with lead-ins will see changes (the byte-identical goldens in acceptance_tests.py use svg_single WITHOUT lead-ins, so they stay green). Runtime +18% on the lead-in pass (font check stays well under 1 min). Prove with acceptance_tests.py 53, export_tests.py 31 (incl. 'lead-ins still start in scrap after reordering'), regression_tests.py 12, GUI selftest, stress_test.py, plus the scratch invariant harness (proto_leadin.check_invariants) which re-verifies pierce>=kerf, standoff held, no crossing, own-hole containment and merge_run ring-index consistency.

findings.title: Kerf floor (0.004 in / 0.10 mm) is never stated numerically where a laser operator sets lead-ins, and is not configurable against their real kerf
findings.evidence: The floor is defined at nameplate_leadin.py:86-87 (HARD_CLEARANCE_IN = 0.004, HARD_CLEARANCE_MM = 0.10). Operator-facing surfaces say only 'never below a kerf' with no number: README_APP.txt:106 (and the copy shipped in dist/SeansFontPrototypingFriend/README.txt:106) and the GUI clearance tooltip at nameplate_gui.py:1924-1928. The one place the number reaches a user is the font-check sub-kerf-holes instruction (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1595-1604 / 917-921), which correctly says 'radius of at least 0.004 in' — but that is the font-fixing report, not the lead-in panel where an operator would compare against their machine's kerf.
