Two consistency wrinkles measured: (a) the mm floor 0.10 mm is 1.6% laxer than the inch floor (0.004 in = 0.1016 mm), so the same job checked in mm units accepts marginally tighter entries; (b) MIN_LEAD (0.008 in / 0.20 mm, nameplate_leadin.py:92-93) has the same rounding.
findings.proposed_fix: Docs-only: state the numbers in the LEAD-INS section of README_APP.txt and in the clear_spin tooltip in nameplate_gui.py (e.g. 'never below 0.004 in / 0.10 mm — check this against your laser's kerf'), sourcing the strings from hard_clearance(unit) so they can never drift. Optionally note the deliberate mm rounding in the nameplate_leadin.py comment block at lines 81-93.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on geometry; prevents an operator with a wider kerf (e.g. 0.006 in fiber on thick steel) from trusting a floor that is below their beam width.
findings.risk: String changes only; GUI selftest (51 checks) confirms no layout/behaviour change.

findings.title: Kerf floor constant is duplicated: nameplate_fontcheck.py:178 hardcodes KERF_IN = 0.004 instead of deriving it from nameplate_leadin
findings.evidence: nameplate_fontcheck.py:178 'KERF_IN = 0.004  # the laser's own floor; see nameplate_leadin' — a second copy of HARD_CLEARANCE_IN. It is used at nameplate_fontcheck.py:254 (preview margin = 4 kerf widths) and :921 (fallback when a report payload lacks floor_in). Meanwhile the same file uses LI.hard_clearance('in') directly at :1583. If HARD_CLEARANCE_IN is ever tuned (e.g. per LEADIN-3 for a wider-kerf machine), the fontcheck copies silently keep 0.004 and the two modules disagree about what 'sub-kerf' means.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_fontcheck.py replace the literal with KERF_IN = LI.hard_clearance('in') (module already imports nameplate_leadin as LI at :1583's scope — hoist the import). No behaviour change today since the values are equal.
findings.accuracy_effect: None today (values identical); removes a future divergence between the lead-in skip rule and the font-check warning threshold.
findings.risk: Import-order only; run the GUI selftest and acceptance_tests.py to confirm no circular-import issue (nameplate_leadin does not import nameplate_fontcheck, so none expected).

findings.title: holes_detail['width'] is actually the inradius — half the physical opening of a slot — and the field name invites a 2x misreading
findings.evidence: _inradius() (nameplate_leadin.py:165-188) returns the largest inset radius; lead_in_report stores it as 'width' (nameplate_leadin.py:481-488). Measured: a 0.007 in wide slit reports width=0.0035 in (scratch patho_leadin.py case S6). Current consumers are consistent with the radius semantics — stress_test.py:283 and acceptance_tests.py:437 compare it against hard_clearance (a radius-like standoff), and the fontcheck user text correctly says 'largest circle that fits... radius' — and the GUI never displays the field, so no user-visible number is wrong today. But the key name plus the docstring phrase 'the honest measure ... is the hole's WIDTH' (nameplate_leadin.py:479-481) will mislead the next consumer that formats it as an opening size.
findings.proposed_fix: Additive: keep 'width' for compatibility but document it as inradius in the lead_in_report docstring (nameplate_leadin.py:392-399), or add a duplicate key 'inradius' with the same value and note that physical slot width ~= 2x this value.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on geometry; prevents a future report/GUI surface from labeling a 0.007 in slit as 0.0035 in wide.
findings.risk: Docstring/extra-key only; acceptance_tests.py and stress_test.py keep reading 'width' unchanged.

findings.title: Outer contours are exempt from the minimum-lead-length floor that holes are held to (not triggerable in practice — observation only)
findings.evidence: Holes reject a lead shorter than the floor at nameplate_leadin.py:470 ('got is None or got[1] < floor'), but outers only check 'got is None' at :508, so a sub-0.008 in outer lead would be emitted and counted as served rather than reported. I could NOT trigger it: 4 stacked names (ADAM/OLIVIA x2, Merriweather) at gaps 0.25 down to 0.01 in all place full 0.100 in outer leads at full 0.012 in standoff, because _usable_length is free to aim the lead along the stack axis or out the ends. Even if it ever fired, the emitted lead still holds >= 1.15x kerf standoff at the pierce (near-zone construction at :287), so the pierce cannot land on the finished edge — the exposure is a pierce blowout unusually close to the part, silently.
findings.proposed_fix: If parity is wanted: in lead_in_report (nameplate_leadin.py:502-517), when an outer's achieved length < floor, still emit it (an outer must always be cut) but count it in a report field so callers can warn — e.g. reuse 'failed' or add 'short_outers'. Not urgent; arguably by design since an outer contour cannot be skipped the way a hole can.
findings.accuracy_effect: None demonstrated on any real or synthetic input tested; closes a theoretical silent-short-lead path for cramped multi-name sheets.
findings.risk: Touches report bookkeeping only; export_tests.py (31) verifies the per-name grouping and cut order still hold, acceptance_tests.py checks the report keys.

strengths: Safety invariants: all 92 shipped lead-ins across ADAM/Adam/OLIVIA in all three fonts (1.0 in cap, GUI defaults) pass every re-verified invariant with zero violations (scratch proto_leadin.py harness): pierce >= 0.004 in kerf floor from ALL material, the far part of every lead holds the standoff actually used, zero material crossing (intersection length <= 1e-6 fu), every hole lead stays inside its own hole polygon, every lead stays >= kerf floor from every OTHER contour, and merge_run ring-index consistency holds on every run — anchor lies on the raw ring edge it claims (< 1e-6 fu) and the traversed contour length equals the ring perimeter to 1e-6, i.e. the past chord-through-the-part bug is absent on all current outputs.

Placement quality (question 1): against an exhaustive 512-1024-sample no-early-break search with identical criteria, the shipped 56-sample search leaves a mean of 0.00 mil and a worst case of 0.2 mil (0.005 mm) of pierce clearance on the table, and at most 1.4 mil of lead length, over every hole and outer of the 9 real documents; no skipped hole was servable and no served hole could have held a higher standoff at any clearance-ladder level. The n_full>=8 early break is a validated shortcut, not an accuracy leak, on the shipped fonts.

Sampling density (measured): holes get 54-488 anchor points each (two entry directions per point), worst spacing 23.1 mil in Merriweather and 13.1/10.5 mil in the Carrie fonts; the per-segment minimum in _candidates makes flattened curves dense regardless of _SAMPLES=56 and is what finds a 0.040 in pocket branching off a 0.012 in slot at full standoff (synthetic S5).

Pathological holes behave: a 0.018 in slit (axis-aligned AND rotated 30 degrees — rotation invariant) gets the ideal end-entry at the correct relaxed standoff 0.0078 in with full 0.100 in length; a crescent matches exhaustive to 0.1 mil; a sub-kerf 0.007 in slit and a 0.015 in triangle are skipped with honest diagnostics (probe=0.1000 in proves the skip is about standoff, not length; width/inradius recorded), never silently dropped. The only found weakness is the tapered wedge (finding LEADIN-2).

Outer lead-ins (question 4): equal to exhaustive on all 9 documents (identical length and room), pierce kept inside doc.bbox as designed, and robust to cramped sheets — 4 stacked names at gaps down to 0.01 in still place full-length, full-standoff outer leads.

Clearance ladder and floors: the ladder correctly bottoms out at the kerf floor (an oversized requested standoff cannot silently kill all lead-ins), a user-requested lead length below MIN_LEAD is honoured rather than excused with a false 'too narrow' (nameplate_leadin.py:419-423), and a requested clearance below the kerf floor is clamped UP to it — consistent with the documented 'never below a kerf' promise.

The near-zone and tolerance hardening documented in the module holds up: the anchor exemption zone is max(clearance*1.15, 1e-6 fu) and the verify tolerance is absolute (_EPS_FU), so a long requested lead-in cannot buy itself permission to cut the part — confirmed by the invariant harness at the 0.004 in floor.

merge_run() contract (pierce -> anchor -> full contour -> anchor as ONE open path) is exactly what reaches the exporters: runs + closed == every contour on all documents tested, and acceptance/export property tests cover it independently.

The golden byte-identical SVG regression uses svg_single (no lead-ins), so the sealed-core guarantee is structurally insulated from any future lead-in tuning — lead-in behaviour is covered by property-based checks instead, which is the right split.
lead_in_report timing at GUI defaults: 35-408 ms per name on real fonts — far inside the <1 min font-check budget, with headroom for the proposed 1.18x adaptive variant.

findings.title: Letter counters are reported as eyelets when an end has no true eyelet (boss-roundness check promised in docstring is not implemented)
findings.evidence: Shipped repro: MerriweatherCut3Black-Engrave-v2.ttf has an eyelet only on the first letter. build_document(font,'Bob',1.0,'in','cap') then measure_eyelets(doc) returns TWO eyelets; report_text prints 'RIGHT EYELET inner diameter 0.2907 in / wall, thinnest 0.0854 in / roundness 0.870' — that hole is the counter of the final 'b' (hole census: circ=0.870 aspect=0.258 frac=0.860 near=0.140, passes all three gates at nameplate_eyelets.py:118-123 and fills the second max_eyelets slot at :133). The module docstring (nameplate_eyelets.py:13-14) says 'the boss around them has to be round as well' — no such gate exists anywhere in measure_eyelets. Discriminating signal measured: true eyelets have boss_spread/r_out = 0.0004/0.177 in = 0.3%; the false 'b' counter has 0.1211/0.348 = 35% (two orders of magnitude separation). Its r_in-vs-r_area disagreement note also fired (>12%). Contamination paths: GUI eyelet table/preview dims (nameplate_gui.py:512+), report_text, and claude_prompt (nameplate_eyelets.py:421-439) which would emit paste-ready font-editing instructions computed from a letter counter. nameplate_brief.py:304 judges eyes[0] (left-most), so today's brief judge is uncontaminated for left-eyelet fonts, but a right-only-eyelet font would judge a counter.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_eyelets.py measure_eyelets, after computing keep/spread (:190-192), add a boss-roundness gate: reject (or mark) a candidate when spread > ~0.30 * r_out. Given the measured 0.3% vs 35% separation, 0.30 is loose enough for any genuine eyelet. To stay additive/safe, prefer a new Eyelet field like confident: bool = True and have report_text/GUI label suspect entries ('this looks like a letter counter, not an eyelet') rather than silently dropping — or gate outright, since no suite pins eyelet output.
findings.accuracy_effect: Eliminates concrete false measurements (ID 0.2907 in, wall 0.0854 in for 'Bob') shown to the user and pasted into font-editing prompts; makes right-end-less fonts report 'no right eyelet' truthfully.
findings.risk: A genuinely non-round boss (heavily fused script eyelet) could be rejected; the fused-stroke synthetics show spread stays ~0 for concentric bosses even at 49% ray escape, so risk is low at threshold 0.30. Proof suites: acceptance_tests.py (53), export_tests.py (31), regression_tests.py (12) contain zero eyelet references (grep verified); GUI selftest 51 checks use Merriweather 'ADAM' whose only (left, true) eyelet has spread 0.1% of r_out and still passes ID<OD — all keep passing.

findings.title: Outer diameter (median of shortest 60% of rays) is biased low by ~1.18x the hole-centre-to-boss-centre offset; exact only for concentric bosses
findings.evidence: Synthetic ground truth (shapely fake docs feeding the real measure_eyelets): concentric annulus ID=1/OD=2/wall=0.5 -> OD error -0.00% (and 0.00% with one stroke at 11/20/30% ray escape and two strokes at 23/33/41/49% escape — the quantile at nameplate_eyelets.py:190-191 is exactly right for its designed case). But eccentric hole (offset 0.3 in boss R=1): OD measured 1.5875 vs 2.0 = -20.62%; true eccentric boss (offset 0.25R): 1.6648 = -16.76%; mild 5% eccentricity: 1.9396 = -3.02% with NO warning note; egg-shaped hole in a perfectly round boss: -4.57% purely from the ray origin sitting at the hole incentre. ID is computed before and independent of the centre (r_in = LI._inradius(poly) at :139) — measured ID error <=0.009% in every case, so centre error distorts OD only. On the three shipped fonts every true eyelet is concentric (offset 0.1-0.2% of R) and shipped OD agrees with an independent least-squares circle fit within 0.0005 in — so this is LATENT, not live. Consequence path: wall_from_diameters=(OD-ID)/2 feeds nameplate_brief.py:309-312 'eyelet wall' judgment at tol=0.0005 in; a future 5%-eccentric eyelet would mis-state the wall by ~0.009 in (~18x tolerance) at a 0.30 in OD eyelet. A trimmed circle fit on the kept ray hit-points measured 0.00% error on ALL eccentric cases (B/E/E2/F) and -0.00% on concentric, with one known limitation: +3.47% on the extreme two-stroke 49%-escape case where the shipped median stays exact.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_eyelets.py measure_eyelets, after the ray cast (:167-192), add a least-squares (Kasa) circle fit over the kept hit points trimmed to radius <= 1.15*median(keep), no expansion pass. Use it as a cross-check: if |fit_R - shipped r_out| is large AND fit residuals are small (points genuinely on a circle), prefer the fit (or at minimum add new optional Eyelet fields outer_d_fit / boss_centre_offset and a corrective note). Selecting by escape fraction (rays > 1.5*r_out) keeps the shipped median for heavily fused bosses where the fit degrades. Fit cost is negligible (measure_eyelets currently runs 95-146 ms/name).
findings.accuracy_effect: OD error on eccentric eyelets drops from -3%..-21% to ~0.0%; wall_from_diameters and the brief's 'eyelet wall' judgment become trustworthy for non-concentric future fonts. Shipped fonts unchanged (<=0.0005 in shift, within current run-to-run ray noise of +-0.0002 in).
findings.risk: Fused-stroke bosses can pollute the fit (+3.5% at 49% escape measured) — mitigated by only trusting the fit when residuals are small / escape fraction low, and by adding the synthetic B/E/F/D/D2 cases as new regression tests. No existing suite pins OD values (verified), GUI selftest only asserts ID < OD.

findings.title: boss_spread and the 'boss is not truly round' note are computed on the truncated kept set, so moderate eccentricity is silently invisible
findings.evidence: spread = keep[-1]-keep[0] over only the shortest-60% rays (nameplate_eyelets.py:192) and the note gate is spread > 0.25*r_out (:219). Measured: at 5% boss eccentricity the OD is already -3.02% wrong (0.009 in at a 0.30 in eyelet, 18x the brief tolerance) yet spread=0.064 < gate 0.242 — no note fires. The note only fires at gross eccentricity (25-30% offset cases B and E did fire). So exactly the regime where the user should be warned but isn't is 3-15% eccentricity.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the eccentricity signal from the full accepted geometry instead of the truncated set: either |circle-fit centre - hole centre| / fit_R (fit from EYE-2) or the spread of all boss rays below an escape threshold, in nameplate_eyelets.py around :192 and :216-221. Keep the existing boss_spread field as-is (additive: new field or reuse note only).
findings.accuracy_effect: The 'outer diameter is an average' warning fires whenever OD bias exceeds roughly the judge tolerance, instead of only at >4x that bias; no measured numbers change.
findings.risk: Purely additive note logic; risk is over-warning on fused script eyelets — threshold against the D/D2 synthetic cases (spread ~0 there) shows fused-but-concentric bosses stay quiet. Existing suites unaffected (no eyelet pins).

findings.title: Docstring promises a boss-roundness requirement that the code does not perform
findings.evidence: nameplate_eyelets.py:13-14: 'candidates are ranked by how circular they are and how close to an end they sit, and the boss around them has to be round as well.' The candidate filter (:110-127) checks hole circularity, hole aspect and end proximity only; nothing about the boss is ever gated. This is the documented-but-missing check that admits the Merriweather 'Bob' counter (EYE-1).
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement the gate (EYE-1's fix makes the docstring true) or correct the docstring to say the boss is measured but not gated. Prefer implementing, since the sentence describes the right design.
findings.accuracy_effect: None by itself; prevents future maintainers from assuming counters are already screened out by boss shape.
findings.risk: None for a docstring edit; if implemented, same risk envelope as EYE-1.

strengths: Inner diameter via LI._inradius bisection (nameplate_leadin.py:165-188) is far inside the brief's 0.0005 in judge tolerance: 30 iterations give 1.48e-7 fu (= 1.03e-10 in) interval on the real TGCarrie eyelet (hole bbox 159 fu, upem 2048), and it agrees with an independent area-based 60-iteration bisection to 6.5e-10 in on the ID. Worst GEOS negative-buffer emptiness noise measured on synthetic n-gons was +2.7e-4 relative (a 96-gon artifact where buffer(-(apothem+1e-4)) returned a 3e-8-area sliver) — even that maps to only ~3e-5 in at the shipped 0.111 in ID, 16x under tolerance.

ID is measured before and independently of the centre estimate, so an eccentric or egg-shaped hole cannot distort it: measured ID error <=0.009% across perfect annulus, eccentric hole (0.3 offset), eccentric boss, ellipse (ID = exactly the minor axis, 0.899994 vs 0.9 truth), and egg-hole cases.

The centre finder buffer(-0.95*r_in).centroid (nameplate_eyelets.py:144-149) recovers the centre of an eccentric CIRCULAR hole exactly (case B: found (1.3000,1.0000) vs truth (1.3,1.0)) and degrades gracefully to the incentre for egg-shaped holes; erosion-based centring is robust to small notches/tabs where the ring meets a stroke.

wall_min (walked hole exterior vs host exterior, :199-213) is essentially exact: errors <=5e-6 units on 720-gon synthetics, 2.7e-4 worst on coarse 96-gon (artwork discretization, not algorithm), +1.4e-4 on the eccentric-boss case whose true wall_min=0.25. The ~75-sample walk (length/r_in*12, capped 24..180) is adequate: eccentric-annulus wall curvature puts sampling error well under 0.0005 in at real scale. wall_min_at is correctly carried for on-screen dimensioning.

BOSS_QUANTILE=0.60 median is exactly right for its designed problem: OD error 0.00% with one stroke escaping 11/20/30% of rays AND two strokes escaping up to 49% of rays, because the median of the kept set is the 30th percentile of all rays, which stays on the boss as long as boss rays exceed ~30%. For concentric bosses (all three shipped fonts, offsets 0.1-0.2% of R) shipped OD matches an independent circle fit within 0.0005 in.

Detection gates work on all three shipped fonts: every true eyelet is accepted (circularity 0.999-1.000, aspect 0.000); TGCarrie script 'O' counter has circularity 0.159 and 'o' counter 0.551-0.544 (rejected); Merriweather 'O' counter is rejected on aspect 0.541. Ovals pass up to ~1.5:1 (ellipse 1.54:1 aspect=0.3506 just over the 0.35 gate), matching script-font tolerance; the r_in-vs-r_area note correctly stays quiet below ~1.25:1 and fires above.

Question 6 (a name like 'OO'): a counter never outranks a real eyelet when the eyelet exists — near_end ranking (:132) structurally favours the outermost holes, and eyelets are always outboard of the first/last letters ('OO' on TGCarrie: eyelets near=0.094/0.095 chosen; counters rejected at the gates anyway; Merriweather 'OO': O counters rejected on aspect). The failure mode requires a MISSING eyelet on one end (see finding EYE-1), not ranking.

END_FRACTION=0.30 correctly rejects mid-word round holes (a synthetic ring fused into the middle of a bar is refused as an eyelet) and single-letter 'O' still finds its real left eyelet at frac 0.187.

Performance: measure_eyelets runs 95-146 ms per name (TGCarrie 'Amelia', Merriweather 'Bob') — a font check stays far under the 1-minute budget, leaving headroom for the proposed circle-fit cross-check.

The brief's judge path (nameplate_brief.py:303-312) uses eyes[0] (left-most) and the shipped fonts carry a genuine left eyelet, so current pass/fail eyelet judgments are computed from real eyelets; the adjustment/claude_prompt math (percent and font-unit scaling, linearity claim) round-trips consistently from ID and wall_from_diameters.

findings.title: join_scan never tests medial-medial or Capital-initial junctions — the junction types most real names are made of
findings.evidence: join_scan (nameplate_fontcheck.py:368-410) builds only lowercase pairs (676) + trigrams behind 10 context letters (6760) = 7436 combos. Because these fonts substitute initial/final forms, a 2-letter string tests init->final glyphs and a trigram tests init->medial->final; a medial->medial junction (interior of any 4+ letter name) and an initial-Capital->medial junction (Name case) are never shaped. Enumeration (scratch cover.py): on shipped TGCarrieSO-v2.otf the scan exercises 1612 distinct glyph junctions, yet 61 of the junctions in 16 common names (Anna n->n, Hannah 4 of 5 junctions, Emma m->m, Bella l->l...) use glyph pairs the scan never tested; Flourish 77, ShineOnScript1 61. Demonstrated false negatives (scratch medial.py): Cervanttis-ExtraBoldEyelet (reference 'Fonts with issues'): full 7436-combo scan reports 354 failing junctions, but a 676-string medial template scan ('a'+x+y+'a', 0.5s) finds 104 failing of which 98 are NEW (e.g. i->e gap 0.0215 em — cuts 'Daniel' apart; b->j 0.0406 em; i->a 0.0417 em), and a 676-string Name-case scan (C+x+'a', 0.4s) finds 8 NEW including B.eyeL->j gap 0.0155 em — the exact junction of 'Bjorn'. On the SHIPPED TGCarrieSOFlourish-v2.otf the Capital scan finds Dleftring->d (type 'Dda', gap 0.0008 em) that join_scan misses. Meanwhile the report prints 'letter-join scan: 7436 of 7436 combinations tested, 0 junction(s) disconnected', which reads as exhaustive. Mitigations that exist: nameplate_pairsheet.py has midlower/midcaplower groups (but no initial-Capital+medial group either — Bjorn's junction is untested there too, GROUP_SPECS at nameplate_pairsheet.py:90-101), and the GUI preview verifies whatever name is actually typed (nameplate_gui.py:2679-2682). But the CLI (which the font-production skill drives) and check_font's verdict pre-approve a font for arbitrary future names.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_fontcheck.py join_scan(), append two template phases to `combos`: medial pairs 'a'+x+y+'a' for all lowercase x,y (676; judge all junctions as name_gaps already does), and Name-case C+x+'a' for all capitals C and lowercase x (676; requires adding uppercase to `have` handling). Measured cost +0.3-0.8s per font (full current scans run 1.7-4.6s); the existing budget/truncation reporting already covers overrun. Purely additive to fontcheck, no nameplate_core change.
findings.accuracy_effect: Removes a demonstrated false-negative class: fonts that pass check_font today but cut real names (Anna, Daniel, Bjorn) into loose pieces would be flagged. On the 3 shipped fonts the added scans produce exactly one new, geometrically true junction (Flourish 'Dda', 1.6 font units) and zero false positives.
findings.risk: Flourish's existing letter-gaps WARNING gains one junction line ('Dda') — truthful but a near-nonexistent name pattern; scan time grows ~15%. No golden SVGs touched (acceptance_tests.py 53 unaffected); export_tests.py 31 and regression_tests.py 12 don't import fontcheck (grep verified). GUI selftest calls font_report_text() so run the 51-check selftest to confirm the report still renders.

findings.title: Wrong-winding counters cut solid metal and no check can see it — checker's fill model is winding-blind, the cut is winding-sensitive
findings.evidence: build_document unions glyphs with skia pathops (nameplate_core.py:432-439, winding fill), but every fontcheck measurement uses Font.filled() (nameplate_core.py:163-181), which resolves holes by containment PARITY and ignores contour direction. Experiment (scratch corrupt.py C4/c4b): in a copy of shipped MerriweatherCut3Black-Engrave-v2.ttf, rewound both counters of O.ini (the glyph 'O' actually shapes to) to match the outer contour's direction. Result: actual cut for 'O' collapses to depths [0] — ZERO holes, the letter lasers as a solid blob; filled() still reports 2 holes; check_font returns ZERO findings and 'letter-join scan: 7436 of 7436, 0 disconnected'. The defect is invisible because O is not in the ADAM/Adam test names (the only place union geometry is inspected) and the join scan's model doesn't share the cut's fill rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a per-glyph check in check_font (nameplate_fontcheck.py, new guarded block): for every letter glyph reachable via cmap + shaped forms, compare skia-union of the glyph (exactly what build_document does: pathops.op(empty, outline, UNION), flatten via _flatten_recording, depth-parity count) against filled() — flag hole-count mismatch or material-area difference >0.5% as ERROR 'counters wound the wrong way: this letter cuts solid'. Prototype in scratch windingfp.py.
findings.accuracy_effect: Catches a silent artwork-destroying defect class (lost counters/eyelet holes). Measured on 287 letter glyphs across the 3 shipped fonts: 0 false positives; the corrupt glyph is uniquely identified (cut holes=0 vs model holes=2, cut area +55%).
findings.risk: Adds ~1-2s per font (one skia op per cached outline; caches already exist). A font with genuinely overlapping same-direction nested rings would be flagged — that is always a drawing error under both TrueType and CFF fill conventions. No core change; run acceptance/export/regression suites plus GUI selftest to confirm (none import the new code path except via check_font).

findings.title: Zero-advance letters (and kern-driven letter order swaps) pass with zero findings while the artwork silently collapses
findings.evidence: Experiment (scratch corrupt.py C1): in a copy of reference ShineOnScript2.ttf, set hmtx advance of 'd' from 474 to 0. check_font: findings = [] — completely clean. The checker's own facts record the damage without noticing it: test name 'Adam' shrank from 3.432 to 2.751 in and lost a hole (5 -> 4) because 'd' and 'a' print stacked on top of each other. Stacked ink always intersects, so name_gaps/join_scan (which only test for NON-touching neighbours, nameplate_fontcheck.py:145-159) can never fire. The same blindness covers class (g): a huge negative GPOS kern that reorders letters keeps ink overlapping, so nothing reports — shape() (nameplate_core.py:208-236) accumulates pen x and no check inspects it.
findings.proposed_fix: Additive check in check_font: (1) every cmap'd letter's hmtx advance must be > 0 (report letter, glyph, gid); (2) shaped pen x positions of the test names and scan strings must be non-decreasing — a regression flags 'letters print out of order / on top of each other' with the offending pair. Both are cheap (no geometry).
findings.accuracy_effect: Turns a silent wrong-artwork case (letters merged/reordered but 'No problems found') into a named ERROR. Measured false-positive risk: 0 — all 52 letters in all 3 shipped fonts have positive advances and all test shapings are monotone.
findings.risk: Fonts that legitimately use zero-advance mark glyphs are not affected (check only letters A-Za-z via cmap). Cursive fonts with slight negative kerning still keep monotone pen positions; only genuine order swaps trip it. Verify with the 3 shipped fonts + GUI selftest.

findings.title: A glyph with contours but zero ink produces 301 misdirected 'extend the exit stroke' orders and never names the real defect
findings.evidence: The empty-glyphs check tests `font.contours(g)` truthiness (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1435), but contours() keeps any ring with >2 points even if collinear/zero-area, while filled() drops rings with area 0 (nameplate_core.py:166) — so the glyph draws nothing yet is not 'empty'. Experiment (scratch corrupt.py C2): replaced 'm' in a ShineOnScript2 copy with a 3-point collinear contour. empty-glyphs does NOT fire; instead the report blames every neighbour: WARNING not-connected ('the break is between: a->mrightring') plus WARNING '301 letter junction(s) do not join' listing Aleftring->mrightring etc. — a work order that tells the editor to lengthen dozens of unrelated strokes when the actual fix is redrawing one glyph. Severity is also understated: the report header says 'Usable, but check the warnings' for a font that cannot cut any name containing m.
findings.proposed_fix: In the empty-outline loop (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1427-1449), treat a glyph as empty when `font.contours(g)` is empty OR the filled area is empty (reuse _filled_cached(font, g): None or .is_empty). Keeps the existing ERROR severity, correct 'draw the outline' instruction, and glyph/gid data.
findings.accuracy_effect: The defect gets its true name (ERROR empty-glyphs on the one glyph) instead of 301 wrong instructions; the claude_prompt work order stops directing edits at healthy glyphs. FP risk measured: every letter glyph in the 3 shipped fonts has non-empty filled ink.
findings.risk: A glyph whose ink is entirely zero-area is unconditionally a defect, so no legitimate font is newly flagged. The 301 junction warnings would largely disappear for such fonts (replaced by one ERROR) — that is the intended change. Re-run GUI selftest; other suites don't touch fontcheck.

findings.title: Caps-only/unicase fonts are not surfaced: shipped Merriweather maps all 26 lowercase to capital glyphs and the report says 'No problems found' with no mention
findings.evidence: fonts/MerriweatherCut3Black-Engrave-v2.ttf: cmap glyph for every one of a-z is IDENTICAL to its capital's glyph (verified: 26/26). check_font output: 'No problems found. This font should work.' The only trace is that both test names measure identically (4.069 x 1.020 in for ADAM and Adam) — data the checker prints but does not interpret. nameplate_core.py's own _measure_basis comment calls this font unicase and documents that its declared sxHeight (1097) is a lie against the real 1486 — trusting metadata here once delivered letters 35% tall. A shop typing 'Adam' gets ADAM-shaped artwork with no warning, and a font editor reading the claude_prompt is never told the lowercase set is intentionally capital.
findings.proposed_fix: In check_font's cmap section (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1361-1407), count letters where cmap[lower] == cmap[upper]; when >= ~20 of the available pairs match, add a fact (and a NOTE with code in CONTEXT_CODES so it stays background in the prompt): 'lowercase is mapped to the capital glyphs (unicase) — typed lowercase renders as capitals'. Data: the count and an example pair.
findings.accuracy_effect: Surfaces a real, currently-invisible property of a shipped production font in the report and the repair prompt (question j answered: it is NOT surfaced today). No geometry changes.
findings.risk: None measurable: TGCarrieSO and Flourish share 0/26 glyphs between cases, so only genuine unicase fonts trigger. As a NOTE it cannot flip a verdict or add repair tasks. GUI selftest re-run to confirm report text renders.

findings.title: GUI 'Check font' runs the entire check twice — 10s instead of 5s, and report vs paste-prompt can disagree when the scan truncates
findings.evidence: nameplate_gui.py:2969 calls font_report_text(path) -> check_font(path).text(), then :2972 calls check_font(path).claude_prompt() again. One check_font on shipped TGCarrieSOFlourish-v2.otf measures 5.1s; claude_prompt() from an existing Report takes 0.002s. So the dialog costs ~10.2s where ~5.1s suffices. Worse for truth: the two runs are independent wall-clock-budgeted scans — on a slower machine or bigger font where the 6s budget truncates, the human report and the paste-prompt can be built from different tested-combo counts and name different junctions.
findings.proposed_fix: In nameplate_gui.py check_font() (:2961-2991), call nameplate_fontcheck.check_font(path) once, keep the Report, and derive both rep.text() and rep.claude_prompt() from it (font_report_text can gain an optional pre-built Report parameter or the dialog can inline the two calls). GUI-only; fontcheck untouched.
findings.accuracy_effect: Guarantees the report and the work order describe the same measured findings; halves the wait behind the busy cursor.
findings.risk: Trivial refactor risk in GUI error handling (the current code intentionally survives prompt-build failure with a placeholder — keep that try/except). Verify with GUI selftest 51 checks.

findings.title: prompt_for_font is dead code with a divergent default budget (12s vs 6s everywhere else)
findings.evidence: nameplate_fontcheck.py:1281 defines prompt_for_font(path, join_scan_budget=12.0); grep across the repo finds no caller. check_font defaults to 6.0 (:1287) and the CLI defaults to 6.0 (:1695). A future caller reaching for the convenience wrapper gets double the scan budget of every other path for no stated reason.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the default to 6.0 (or delete the function). One-line, no behavior change for any current caller since none exist.
findings.accuracy_effect: None today; prevents a future inconsistency where the prompt path tests more combos than the report path and they disagree.
findings.risk: None — no callers. Suites unaffected.

findings.title: colr-version ERROR contradicts the module's own severity definition — a COLR v1 font still cuts, it only loses engraving
findings.evidence: nameplate_fontcheck.py:22-25 defines ERROR as 'the font cannot produce a usable cut file until this is fixed'. The colr-version finding (:1458-1466) is ERROR, yet its own detail says only 'no engraving will be produced' — the cut outline path is unaffected (engrave extraction at nameplate_core.py:459-489 simply finds no v0 layers; cutting proceeds). The GUI probe then declares the font 'cannot be used as it is' (nameplate_gui.py:436) when cut-only use is fine. All other severities audited against runs on 6 fonts came out correct: punctuation demoted to fact, cut-only demoted to fact, both 'no engrave lines' engine notes suppressed (the old engrave-lines mistake is fixed and did not overshoot — the 'marks engrave lines but none landed' variant still surfaces), join-scan-partial NOTE with 'untested is not a pass' wording, missing-space WARNING, missing-letters ERROR only above 26.
findings.proposed_fix: Either downgrade colr-version to WARNING with text 'cuts fine, engraving lost until re-exported as COLR v0', or keep ERROR deliberately as a blocking policy and amend the detail to say the block is intentional. Judgment call for Sean; one string/severity constant in nameplate_fontcheck.py.
findings.accuracy_effect: Report wording matches reality for COLR v1 fonts; no geometric change.
findings.risk: Downgrading means a v1 engrave font can be used cut-only without a blocking flag — if the engraving IS the product (Merriweather Engrave line), Sean may prefer the block. Hence presented as a choice, not a defect fix.

strengths: CLI verified: the font-production skill's claim is accurate. nameplate_fontcheck.py accepts --prompt (plus undocumented -p alias), --no-join-scan (sets budget to 0 and still says so rather than passing silently), --budget=SECONDS (default 6.0); unknown option or non-numeric budget prints usage and exits 2; no paths exits 2; ERROR findings exit 1; usable/warnings exit 0. Output survives cp1252 consoles via _emit (nameplate_fontcheck.py:1676-1689).

join_scan budget truth (question 3): the real combo count is 7436 (676 pairs + 10 contexts x 676 trigrams), not 2704, and the default 6s budget completed 7436/7436 on ALL six fonts tested (scan alone 1.7-4.6s; 3-font CLI run 9.5s total). The sub-kerf sliver and multi-piece checks measure the REAL built artwork (nameplate_leadin rings on build_document output), state the kerf floor in both font units and inches, name the two glyphs forming each sliver with per-glyph coordinates, and the not-connected finding carries full junction_details for the work order — verified on Cervanttis (3 pieces for ADAM, junctions named with gaps in inches).

Report/prompt architecture holds up under abuse: unreadable files produce a short do-not-edit prompt instead of invented font facts (verified with a junk .ttf, exit 1); every check is individually exception-guarded so one broken table cannot eat the other findings; Finding.instruction falls back to prose that admits it could not measure.

findings.title: Five button handlers block the GUI thread: 9.9 s / 8.8 s / 3.5 s / 0.6 s / 0.2 s measured freezes
findings.evidence: Measured end-to-end, statement-for-statement as the handlers run, on TGCarrieSOFlourish-v2.otf ('Olivia' @ 25 mm cap): check_font (gui.py:2961) 9.92 s; generate_prompts (gui.py:2994; full check 5.1 s + analyse_pairs 3.0 s + thickness/eyelet prompts) 8.81 s; show_pair_sheets (gui.py:3113; analyse_pairs dominates) 3.50 s; measure_thickness (gui.py:2909) 0.64 s; measure_eyelets/eyelet_report_text (gui.py:2892/2868) 0.22 s. All five run on the GUI thread under QApplication.setOverrideCursor — the window is frozen the whole time (no repaint, no cancel, Windows may declare 'Not Responding' past 5 s). Note measure_thickness and eyelet_report_text also re-open a fresh Font and rebuild the doc on the GUI thread even though PreviewWorker has res.eyelets/thin_spots cached.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the existing worker pattern (do NOT reuse the preview thread — a 10 s check would starve typing previews): add ReportWorker(QObject) on its own long-lived QThread, started lazily beside _start_preview_thread (gui.py:2374). Signals: requestReport = Signal(int, str, str, str, float, str, str, float, float, float) carrying (req_id, kind in {'check','prompts','pairs','thickness','eyelets'}, font_path, name, height, unit, basis, thin_target, eye_id, eye_wall); reportReady = Signal(int, str, object); reportFailed = Signal(int, str, str). Worker opens a FRESH Font per job and hands it over with the result for PairSheetDialog (ownership transfer, never concurrent use — respects the module's 'Font objects are not thread-safe' rule; the current code already passes a GUI-built Font into the dialog). Cancellation: reuse the req_id discipline — MainWindow keeps _last_report_id, stale results dropped on arrival; the triggering button is disabled and relabeled 'Checking… ' while a job runs (these are click-driven, one in flight is enough; a Cancel just bumps _last_report_id). The wait cursor becomes: button disabled + status text + normal cursor; on reportReady open the exact same TextDialog/PromptsDialog/PairSheetDialog. --selftest compatibility: _quiet already stores _last_report/_last_prompt_sections and the selftest has pump(cond) (gui.py:3229) to wait on signals.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on geometry or report content — identical functions run with identical inputs, off-thread. Usability accuracy improves: the user can keep typing and the app can never be killed mid-check by an impatient 'Not Responding' dialog. Font check stays well under the 1-minute usability bar (worst 5 s after GUI-1's de-duplication).
findings.risk: Thread-affinity mistakes (building widgets from the worker) — avoided by emitting plain data + transferring the Font. Regression proof: acceptance_tests.py 53, export_tests.py 31, regression_tests.py 12 (untouched engine), plus GUI selftest 51 checks which exercise check_font, prompts, pair sheets, thickness and eyelet paths in _quiet mode.

findings.title: PreviewWorker computes every stale queued build — typing 9 keystrokes runs 9 full builds, preview lags 1.8 s behind the last key
findings.evidence: Experiment against the real PreviewWorker (TGCarrieSOFlourish, thin+eyelet toggles on, 9 keystrokes 'Olivia's!' at 180 ms apart — just above the 150 ms debounce so every keystroke fires _do_preview, exactly like real typing): all 9 requests were built serially (finish times 0.23/0.54/0.87/1.23/1.63/2.06/2.48/2.93/3.45 s), 8 results fully computed then discarded by the req_id check in _preview_ready (gui.py:2664), and the preview the user sees landed 1.81 s AFTER the last keystroke. Per-build cost with toggles on: ~420 ms on the Carrie fonts (build_document ~28 ms + find_thin_spots ~282 ms + measure_eyelets ~127 ms), ~600 ms with thicken_preview overlay active. The queued-connection signal (gui.py:2378) delivers every emit; the debounce timer (DEBOUNCE_MS=150, gui.py:2210-2213) only collapses keystrokes faster than 150 ms.
findings.proposed_fix: Skip-to-latest inside the worker without touching the req_id contract: (1) give PreviewWorker an int attribute latest_req = 0; (2) in _do_preview (gui.py:2649-2651), after self._last_preview_id = self._req, also set self._preview_worker.latest_req = self._req — a cross-thread int attribute write is GIL-atomic and needs no lock; (3) first line of PreviewWorker.build(): if req_id != self.latest_req: return (optionally also emit a new 'skipped' signal, and re-check between the build/thin/eyelet stages to abandon mid-build). _preview_ready keeps its existing req_id guard as the backstop. IMPORTANT: track only preview ids — _font_changed shares the _req counter for probes (gui.py:2435), which is why latest_req must be assigned from _last_preview_id, never from _req inside probe paths.
findings.accuracy_effect: None — skipped builds are precisely the ones _preview_ready already throws away; the surviving result is bit-identical. Perceived accuracy improves: the on-screen numbers (size, thin spot, eyelet table) stop trailing seconds behind what is typed.
findings.risk: If latest_req were set for probe requests too, previews could be wrongly skipped — the fix above avoids that by construction. Prove with: rerun of the queue experiment (expect ~2 builds instead of 9), GUI selftest 51 checks (its pump() waits on the final request id, unaffected), acceptance/export/regression suites untouched.

findings.title: Crash handling: worker-thread exceptions pop a QMessageBox on the wrong thread, and the only crash record (startup.log) is erased at the next launch
findings.evidence: Tested on PySide6 6.11.1 / Python 3.12.10 with the app's exact hook pattern: unhandled exceptions in slots on BOTH the GUI thread and a worker QThread route through sys.excepthook (event loop and worker survive, process does not abort) — so the hook at nameplate_gui.py:3923-3931 does fire for worker slots. BUT the hook runs ON the raising thread: measured thread name 'Dummy-1', main=False for a worker-slot raise. The hook then calls QMessageBox.critical(None, ...) — creating a widget and spinning a modal event loop on a non-GUI thread, which Qt forbids (it happened not to raise under the offscreen platform; on the real windows platform this is undefined behavior — crash or freeze — and it blocks the worker thread either way). Second gap: the hook logs 'UNCAUGHT'+traceback to startup.log, but main() truncates startup.log on every launch (gui.py:3883, open(_LOG, 'w')), so the crash evidence is destroyed by the user's first reflex — relaunching. Third gap: no faulthandler, so a native crash in Qt/skia-pathops/uharfbuzz leaves nothing at all. (PreviewWorker.build/probe and ExportWorker.run each have their own try/except -> failed signal, so the hook is only the backstop for GUI-side slots like _preview_ready — good.)
findings.proposed_fix: Three small additions in nameplate_gui.py main(): (1) crash file — in excepthook, before any dialog, write crash_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.txt beside startup.log (reuse _log_path()'s folder fallback) containing app version/build stamp (finding GUI-5), python/PySide6 versions, the traceback, and best-effort context (current font path, caret name, height/unit/basis); keep only the newest 10. (2) thread-safe dialog — create a CrashRelay(QObject) on the GUI thread with sig = Signal(str) connected to the QMessageBox-shower; the hook emits relay.sig.emit(msg) (queued, safe from any thread) instead of building the box in place. (3) native crashes — before QApplication, faulthandler.enable(file=open(crash_native.log path, 'a')) with the handle kept referenced for process lifetime. startup.log keeps its truncate-per-launch behavior; crashes now live in their own files.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on output. Diagnosability: a report of 'it crashed yesterday' becomes actionable — today the evidence is gone after one relaunch, and a worker-slot crash may take the whole app down with it.
findings.risk: Excepthook must never raise (wrap everything, as the current one does). faulthandler holds one file handle. Prove with: the crash experiment scripts rerun against the patched file, GUI selftest 51 (hook not installed on the selftest path, unchanged), verify_release.ps1.

findings.title: No build manifest, no version constant, no in-GUI health surface — the shipped exe cannot prove which code it was built from
findings.evidence: Grep of nameplate_gui.py: no APP_VERSION/__version__ anywhere; no 'About' or health UI (only APP_NAME at gui.py:50). installer.iss hardcodes AppVer '1.0.0' (line 18) disconnected from anything. build_all.ps1 writes no stamp of what it built. (2) nameplate_gui.py: read_build_info() checking sys._MEIPASS then BASE; an 'About' QPushButton in the top font row opening the existing TextDialog with: app name/version/stamp/built date; python, PySide6+Qt (qVersion), fontTools, uharfbuzz, skia-pathops, shapely versions via importlib.metadata.version; BASE, FONTS_DIR, SETTINGS_PATH, startup.log path; font file count; a settings-write probe result. (3) _selftest_body: out() the same block in the header. (4) verify_release.ps1: recompute the stamp from the source tree and Check it equals the stamp in selftest_report.txt — this is the check that catches a stale zip. (5) installer.iss: generate '#define AppVer' from build_info.json via an .iss include written by build_all, so the version lives in one place.
findings.accuracy_effect: Indirect but real: eliminates the 'wrong build in the shop' failure mode — a plate cut from an exe that predates a geometry fix is an accuracy incident this manifest makes detectable in one glance at About or one selftest line.
findings.risk: Selftest report gains lines — verify_release.ps1 greps specific strings and is unaffected by additions (verify by running it). GUI selftest count grows only if a check is added, keep it additive. Engine untouched; all 4 suites must stay green.

findings.title: Install guarantees: current state is solid for a solo shop; code signing is optional — Azure Trusted Signing is the only economically sane option, and two zero-cost hardenings are available
findings.evidence: installer.iss audit: per-user install to {localappdata}\Programs (correct, since fonts/ and settings.json must be writable next to the exe — comment lines 9-14), PrivilegesRequired=lowest (no UAC), fixed AppId so re-runs upgrade in place (line 23), user-added fonts preserved on uninstall (UninstallDelete lines 67-75), MinVersion 10.0, x64 only — all appropriate. No SignTool directive: nothing is signed. INSTALL.txt already documents SmartScreen 'More info > Run anyway' (lines 51-55, 168-169) and the ~260-char long-path pitfall (line 155). verify_release.ps1 genuinely tests cold-machine behavior (env stripped to system dirs, PATH = system32 only, Explorer-style extraction).
findings.proposed_fix: Signing options for a solo shop, honestly: (a) none (today) — free; SmartScreen prompt once per machine, already documented; fine for an internal tool on 2-3 shop PCs. (b) self-signed — free, ~1 h; does NOTHING for SmartScreen (reputation is CA-anchored); only worthwhile if the cert is pushed to Trusted Publishers on the shop PCs, which buys a named publisher line, not less friction. (c) standard OV cert — ~$100-400/yr and since June 2023 CA/B rules force the key onto a hardware token or cloud HSM; SmartScreen reputation still accrues slowly, so the prompt does not vanish on day one. (d) EV — ~$300-700/yr + token; fastest reputation; overkill here. (e) Azure Trusted Signing — $9.99/month, Microsoft-issued short-lived certs, integrates with signtool, best reputation-per-dollar; needs an Azure tenant and identity validation. Recommendation: stay unsigned for now; instead add two zero-cost hardenings to build_all.ps1/INSTALL.txt: (1) emit SHA256SUMS.txt beside the three artifacts (Get-FileHash) so a copied zip can be verified on the target PC; (2) INSTALL.txt tip — right-click the downloaded zip > Properties > Unblock BEFORE Extract All, which strips Mark-of-the-Web from everything inside in one step (Extract All otherwise propagates MotW to every extracted file). Also prefer distributing the installer or onedir zip over the single-file exe: onefile self-extracts to %TEMP% at every launch and has the worst PyInstaller AV false-positive rate.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on geometry. Integrity: checksums make 'the zip got corrupted/quarantined in transit' detectable instead of manifesting as mystery startup failures.
findings.risk: None — documentation plus two additive build-script lines. verify_release.ps1 rerun proves the zip is unchanged.

findings.title: settings.json migration is safe in every direction except one: a FUTURE bool setting is silently dropped by an older app and lost on the next save
findings.evidence: Proven by experiment against the real load_settings/save_settings (SETTINGS_PATH monkeypatched to scratch; no app files touched). OLD file missing new keys: loads verbatim; _restore_prefs (gui.py:2282-2342) guards every read with .get + isinstance so missing keys fall to widget defaults — clean. Wrong-typed known keys ({"font_path":123, "height":true, "formats":"svg", "lead_in":"yes"}): all dropped, rest kept — clean, including the bool-subclass-of-int trap (gui.py:111-114). Corrupt JSON / top-level list / missing file: {} — clean. FUTURE file with unknown keys: str/num/list/dict values are KEPT (want=object at gui.py:110, isinstance always true) and survive a save round-trip — good downgrade behavior; but an unknown BOOL key ('new_bool_setting': true) is dropped at load, because line 113 'isinstance(v, bool) and want is not bool' fires for every unknown key (want is object). Round-trip proof: keys before ['height','new_bool_setting',...] -> after save, LOST: ['new_bool_setting']. So running an old exe once against a newer settings.json permanently erases every newer bool preference.
findings.proposed_fix: One-line change in load_settings (gui.py:113): make the bool guard apply only to KNOWN keys — 'if k in _SETTING_TYPES and isinstance(v, bool) and want is not bool: continue'. Unknown bools then pass the isinstance(v, object) check like every other unknown type and round-trip intact.
findings.accuracy_effect: None on geometry. Prevents silent loss of future preferences (e.g. a hypothetical v2 'eye_show_wall': true) when versions are mixed across the shop's PCs via the synced settings.json the docstring itself anticipates.
findings.risk: Known keys keep the exact current behavior (the bool-vs-int protection is untouched for them). Prove with the settings experiment script rerun (all 8 cases) + GUI selftest 51.

strengths: Preview/export threading architecture is correct where it exists: build_document never runs on the GUI thread; PreviewWorker is a single long-lived thread owning its own Font cache with mtime/size invalidation plus an explicit forget() for timestamp-preserving font replacements (nameplate_gui.py:388-413); ExportWorker gets a fresh thread and its own Font per job with a full try/except -> failed signal and an overlap check before writing (gui.py:564-642).

The req_id stale-result discipline is implemented correctly at every receiving slot: _preview_ready and _preview_failed drop non-latest ids (gui.py:2664, 2688), and _font_info_ready additionally path-normalizes before accepting (gui.py:2442) — no stale preview can ever overwrite a newer one on screen.

The automatic per-selection font probe does NOT freeze the GUI: it runs on the preview worker with join_scan_budget=0.0 (gui.py:415-441), measured at 158-341 ms on the three shipped fonts — the design note in the code ('the letter-pair scan is skipped here, it costs seconds') matches the measurements exactly.

load_settings type-gating is correct for all current keys, including the subtle bool-is-a-subclass-of-int trap ({"height": true} is rejected); old settings.json files load cleanly with widget defaults filling gaps; corrupt files, wrong top-level types and missing files all degrade to {} without error — proven by experiment for 8 cases (only exception filed as SET-1).

The GUI eyelet table can never disagree with the eyelet report: _fill_eyelet_table's want-OD formula ((t_id or inner_d) + 2*(t_wall or wall_from_diameters), gui.py:2835) is arithmetically identical to nameplate_eyelets.adjustment (nameplate_eyelets.py:303-308, verified m_od = inner + 2*wall_from_diameters = outer_d), and the overlay ring radius base_id/2 + wall matches the same math (gui.py:538-541). Blank want/change cells for untargeted rows correctly distinguish 'not asked' from 'already right'.

Startup diagnosability is unusually thorough for a desktop tool: per-phase startup.log with LOCALAPPDATA fallback for read-only folders, fatal() that drops the splash first and falls back to a raw Win32 MessageBox when Qt itself is broken, --diagnose walking the startup stepwise, selftest write-probing its outdir and falling back to temp, and os._exit after selftest to prevent the live-QThread hang it documents (gui.py:148-213, 3170-3215, 3864-3877).

verify_release.ps1 is a genuine cold-machine test: environment stripped to system dirs with PATH=system32 only, Explorer-equivalent zip extraction, exit-code and report assertions, per-name-group cutting-order grep on the produced SVG (engrave -> inner -> outline), PDF header check, and no-text/no-rect guarantee that preview guides never reach a cut file.

installer.iss makes the right calls for this app's constraints: per-user {localappdata}\Programs install because fonts/ and settings.json must be writable next to the exe, PrivilegesRequired=lowest (no UAC on locked-down shop PCs), fixed AppId for in-place upgrades, and an uninstall that removes runtime files but deliberately preserves user-added fonts.

PySide6 6.11.1 (the installed version) routes unhandled slot exceptions from BOTH GUI and worker threads through the installed sys.excepthook and keeps the event loop and worker threads alive — verified by experiment — so the existing hook plus the workers' own try/except nets mean no exception class is currently invisible; the gaps are the wrong-thread dialog and log truncation filed in GUI-4, not missing coverage.
